- `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is replaced with the runner's own `rustup`. The
  action is versioned by branch, so there is no release for a pin to name or
  for Dependabot to follow. Toolchains and components are unchanged.
- `ci.yml` declares `permissions: contents: read`. Nothing in it writes.
- `publish.yml` grants `id-token: write` to the publish job rather than the
  whole workflow, and runs that job in the `crates-io` environment. The
  environment's protection rules are repository settings and binding it in the
  crate's Trusted Publishing configuration is a crates.io setting; neither is
  part of this change. Naming the environment first is safe, because a Trusted

* ci: keep pinned actions and dependencies current with Dependabot

A SHA pin does not move on its own. Dependabot proposes a new pin, and
rewrites the version comment beside it, when an action publishes a release.

Weekly for `github-actions`, grouped into a single pull request, and weekly for
`cargo`. Both hold a new release back for seven days before proposing it, so a
retagged or withdrawn release has time to be noticed; security updates are not

title: feat(confirm): reject expired confirm/response documents
body:
feat(confirm): reject expired confirm/response documents

TrustTaskDocument.expiresAt and .issuedAt were declared and signed by the
wallet but never read, so verifyConfirmResponse accepted a decision of any age
— the SDK delegated all timeliness to the RP's server-side challenge binding.
Check them as defense in depth, after the proof has verified (they are signed
fields, so they mean nothing before that):

- A document whose expiresAt has passed fails with the new `expired` reason. An
  unparseable expiresAt is malformed_payload rather than silently ignored.
- New optional maxAgeSecs bounds how far issuedAt may lie behind now; with it
  set, a missing or unparseable issuedAt also fails `expired` (fail closed —
  the caller asked for an age bound).
- New optional now supplies the clock reading, defaulting to the current time,
  so a caller can pin one reading across several verifications and tests need
  no fake timers.

Both parameters are optional and `expired` is an added reason value, so this is
additive for existing callers. The API docs and README keep the note that these
checks cannot replace the caller's own controls: locating the pending request by
challenge, consuming it single-use and persisting the decision remain the
authoritative single-use and freshness mechanism.

Tests: 53 pass (was 47). Covers expiresAt in the past -> expired, still in the
future -> verifies, absent -> verifies, unparseable -> malformed_payload, and
maxAgeSecs over/under the document's age plus the no-issuedAt case.

title: fix(did): refuse to resolve a did:webvh hosted on a local-only name or non-public address
body:
## Why

The consent prompt resolves the `rpDid` a page supplies (`verifyDid`), and the vault panel resolves a principal DID to derive its signing key (`deriveSigningKeyId`). Resolving a did:webvh fetches its log from the host the DID names. Whoever wrote the DID chose that host, and this path deliberately runs with no host grant (see `host-permissions.ts`). So a page could make the extension send requests to loopback, the local network or a cloud metadata address while the prompt was open.

`didwebvh-ts` refuses plain dotted-quad and colon-form IPv6 literals. It does not refuse local-only names, or the other IPv4 spellings that the URL parser accepts and rewrites into a private address.

## Change

- New `packages/core/src/did/egress-guard.ts`. `assertResolvableWebvhHost(did)` works in three steps:
  - It takes the host with `didWebvhDomain` and percent-decodes it.
  - It parses the host with the WHATWG URL parser, the same parser the resolver uses to build its fetch URL. This strips the port and canonicalises numeric forms.
  - It throws `BlockedEndpointError` (`code: "E_BLOCKED_ENDPOINT"`, `reason: "private_address" | "private_name" | "invalid_url"`) for any of the following:
    - IPv4 outside public space: this-network, loopback, RFC 1918, link-local, CGNAT, IETF protocol assignments, documentation, benchmarking, multicast, reserved and broadcast.
    - IPv6 loopback and unspecified, ULA, link-local, site-local, multicast, documentation, and IPv4-mapped, IPv4-compatible, NAT64 and 6to4 forms (judged by the embedded IPv4 address).
    - `localhost`, `local`, `internal` and `home.arpa`, the names under them, and single-label names.
    - A host that does not parse, or that carries userinfo, a path, a query, a fragment, a second layer of percent-encoding, or whitespace.

  The guard does not use `didwebvh-ts`'s own IP check. Its ranges, names, error code and reason strings match `net-guard.js` in the next `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` release, so it can be swapped for that module once it ships.
- `verifyDid` and `deriveSigningKeyId` call the guard for did:webvh before resolving. A refusal comes back in each function's existing failure shape: `resolved: false` plus `error`, and `candidates: []` plus `error`. Neither function throws.
- Both functions gain an optional `{ resolveDid }` option, named like `VerifyTrustTaskProofOptions.resolveDid`, so tests can prove the resolver is never reached. Existing callers are unchanged.
- `host-permissions.ts`: the comment on the grant exemption for DID resolution now says the host is judged before anything is fetched.

## User-visible behaviour

- **Consent prompt:** a DID with a refused host shows the existing "Verification failed" badge. The detail line reads, for example: "Could not resolve this DID: the DID's host localhost is a local-network name, not a public internet host, so it was not contacted." No agent name is shown.
- **Vault panel:** the same message appears as the signing-key derivation error, and nothing is auto-filled.
- **Other screens:** `useAgentNames` shows no name, as for any DID that does not resolve.
- DIDs on public hosts behave as before.

## Not covered

- A public name that resolves to a private address. An extension has no DNS API, so this needs resolution somewhere that can see the address.
- Other resolution paths in `packages/core/src/didcomm/index.ts`: mediator, key agreement, and the `resolveDidDocument` that Trust-Task proof verification uses. Also not covered: nested did:webvh verification methods that `didwebvh-ts` fetches itself. These should move to the shared guard once `@openvtc/vti-didcomm-js` ships it.
- Approve in the consent window is still not gated on verification succeeding. That is unchanged here.
- `proxyFetch` and gateway registration.

## Tests

`packages/core/tests/did.egress-guard.mjs` (node:test):

- The guard refuses local-only names, alternate numeric IPv4 spellings, non-public IPv4 and IPv6 literals, and malformed hosts. It passes public names, including ones with a blocked word as a label (`localhost.example.com`), and addresses just outside the blocked ranges.
- `verifyDid` and `deriveSigningKeyId` return their failure shape for every refused host without calling an injected resolver. Both still call the resolver for a public host.
- With the real resolver and a recording `fetch`, refused hosts produce no request, while a public host does.

Results: every CI step passed locally on Node 26.7.0, starting from a cold build (no `dist` or build info):

- `npm run lint`
- `npm run build`
- `npm test`: tsp-js 51, core 609, extension 590, reviewer-demo 9, with no failures
- the MV3 single-bundle and bundle-surface assertions
- Web Store packaging and the zip checks

The Node 24 leg of the matrix was not run locally.

To check the tests are not vacuous, the guard calls were removed from the built output. The three wiring tests then failed as expected.

## Pre-merge checklist

```
- [x] No new reqwest::Client::new() / bare fetch(); all clients have finite timeouts (R1.2) — no new network call; the guard is synchronous
- [x] No lock held across a network await (R1.3) — n/a
- [x] No local state committed before its remote effect, or the flow is resumable with an idempotency key (R2.1) — n/a, no state
- [x] Every retry is bounded + backed off; non-idempotent ops are not blind-retried (R1.4) — n/a
- [x] Accept/poll/listen loops survive transient errors (R1.5) — n/a
- [x] Acks/deletes happen only after durable handoff (R1.6) — n/a
- [x] New/changed wire types: camelCase, deny_unknown_fields where security-relevant, schema registered, all consumers (incl. JS) updated (R3.*) — no wire change; the bridge's VerifyRpDidResult is unchanged
- [x] Config absence = most restrictive; fail-closed if enforcement can't start (R5.*) — no configuration; a host that cannot be parsed is refused
- [x] Logs/status claim only what was verified; background-job failures are surfaced (R6.*) — the message says the host was not contacted
- [x] "Process dies on the next line" answered for every mutation touched (R2.1) — n/a, no mutation
- [x] Deviations from this guide flagged explicitly with rule numbers — R3.7: the stable code is on the thrown error, but only the message crosses the bridge; the UI renders it and does not branch on it
```

title: fix(confirm): require a matching recipient when an audience is expected
body:
fix(confirm): require a matching recipient when an audience is expected

verifyConfirmResponse only compared doc.recipient against params.audience when
both were present, so a confirm/response carrying no recipient passed the
audience check by omission. Such a response is bound to no relying party: a
wallet-signed decision could be re-presented to a different RP, which accepts
it unless it binds the challenge to the pending confirm server-side.

Drop the doc.recipient !== undefined escape. Passing audience now asserts that
the document carries a recipient equal to it; a missing or different recipient
fails with the existing audience_mismatch reason, so the failure taxonomy is
unchanged. Callers that pass no audience keep the previous behaviour — the
parameter docs and README now recommend always passing it.

Tests: 47 pass (was 44). test/confirm.test.ts grows a signed-response helper
(a fresh holder key, so fields the wallet fixture fixes can be varied and the
proof still verifies) and covers recipient-absent-with-audience ->
audience_mismatch, recipient-absent-without-audience -> still verifies, and
recipient-matches-audience -> verifies.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: ci: pin actions, narrow tokens and keep dependency builds away from publishing
body:
## Summary

Hardens the workflows that publish crates and build the `verify-trust` binaries the composite action downloads:

- every `uses:` pinned to a full commit SHA, with Dependabot keeping the pins current;
- least-privilege `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions in every workflow;
- no dependency cache in release builds;
- `publish.yml` split so dependency build scripts never run in the job holding the crates.io OIDC permission;
- build-provenance attestations for release tarballs.

No Rust source changes.

## Changes

### Action pinning (`ci.yml`, `verify-trust.yml`, `publish.yml`, `release.yml`)

All pins were resolved with `gh api` on the day of this change. Annotated tags were dereferenced to their commits, and each SHA matches the release's floating major tag.

| Action | SHA | Release |
|---|---|---|
| actions/checkout | `3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1` | v7.0.1 |
| actions/upload-artifact | `043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a` | v7.0.1 |
| actions/download-artifact | `3e5f45b2cfb9172054b4087a40e8e0b5a5461e7c` | v8.0.1 |
| Swatinem/rust-cache (CI only) | `6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6` | v2.9.2 |
| softprops/action-gh-release | `efb35369e0ad2afab669f228072c1b0d510eae64` | v3.0.3 |
| rust-lang/crates-io-auth-action | `c6f97d42243bad5fab37ca0427f495c86d5b1a18` | v1.0.5 (also the `v1` branch tip) |
| actions/attest-build-provenance (new) | `4d101475d8b20a2381f78447822ac1eab6504dd8` | v4.2.2 |

- **Rust toolchain.** `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` is replaced by `rustup toolchain install … --profile minimal` plus `rustup default`, using the rustup already on hosted runners. The action is only referenced by branch, so a pin would never get a Dependabot update. The MSRV job still installs 1.95.0. Release builds add `--target` for the matrix target.
- **`action-selftest.yml`** was already pinned and is unchanged.
- **`.github/dependabot.yml`** (new):
  - `github-actions`, weekly, `cooldown.default-days: 7`, `directories: ["/", "/.github/actions/verify-trust"]`, grouped into one PR;
  - `cargo`, weekly, 7-day cooldown.

### Token permissions

- `ci.yml`, `verify-trust.yml` and `release.yml` now set top-level `permissions: contents: read`. `publish.yml` already did.
- `release.yml`:
  - `contents: write` only on the `release` job;
  - `id-token: write` and `attestations: write` only on the `build` job, for the attestation.
- Checkouts that never push set `persist-credentials: false`.

### `release.yml`

- `Swatinem/rust-cache` is removed from the build job. A release binary is built from a clean target directory, not from a cache another workflow run could have written.
- New step `actions/attest-build-provenance` over `verify-trust-<target>.tar.gz`. It runs only when `github.ref` is a `v*` tag. A manual dispatch is a dry run and attests nothing, so no attestation exists for a build of an arbitrary branch.
- The `release` job declares `environment: release`, so reviewers and a tag rule configured on that environment apply to it.
- `matrix.target` and `runner.os` reach the shell through `env:` (`TARGET`, `RUNNER_OS`) instead of `${{ }}` in `run:`.

### `publish.yml`

| Job | Token | Environment | Runs | Does |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `package` | `contents: read`, no OIDC | none | always | `cargo package --workspace --locked`: packages all three crates and compiles each from its tarball. This is where dependency build scripts run. |
| `publish` | `contents: read`, `id-token: write` | `crates-io` | `needs: package`, and only if `github.ref` starts with `refs/tags/v` | The existing resumable loop, now `cargo publish -p <crate> --locked --no-verify`. It compiles nothing. The system-dependency install step is gone because nothing is built. |

**Choice: publishing is restricted to tag refs.** The alternative was to make `workflow_dispatch` a dry run. Reasons for the choice:

- The only legitimate publish is of a tagged version. The `crates-io` environment's deployment rule (`v*.*.*` tags, see admin steps) enforces the same thing on the server side. The `if:` alone could be edited on a branch; the environment rule and the crates.io environment binding cannot.
- A publish that fails partway has to be retried against the same tag. That is why the loop skips crates already uploaded. Dispatching the workflow on the tag, or re-running the failed run, keeps that recovery path. A dispatch-is-always-dry-run design would remove it.
- A dispatch on a branch still does something useful: it runs `package` only, which is a full packaging dry run.

**`cargo package --workspace` with unpublished sibling versions.** cargo packages the workspace members into a local overlay registry and resolves internal dependencies from it (`Unpacking vgi-core … (registry target/package/tmp-registry)`), so `verify-trust` and `did-git-sign` verify against the vgi-core being released, not the crates.io copy. I checked this locally with cargo 1.98.1 in two cases:

- this tree at 0.4.8, which is already on crates.io;
- a scratch copy with the workspace version and the `vgi-core` requirement bumped to 0.9.99, which is unpublished. `cargo package --workspace --locked` packaged and verified all three crates (exit 0).

## Verification

- `python3` + PyYAML parses all five workflows, `dependabot.yml` and `action.yml`. The parsed permissions, environments, `if:` and `needs:` per job match the tables above.
- `grep -rnE 'uses: *[^ .][^ ]*@' .github | grep -vE '@[0-9a-f]{40}( |$)'` prints nothing.
- `cargo package --workspace --locked`: exit 0 (see above).
- actionlint and zizmor were not available locally. Worth running them before merging.

## Settings to apply (not doable in code)

1. **Tag ruleset** on `refs/tags/v*`: restrict creation, update and deletion, with bypass for repository admins (or the maintainers team) only. Today any writer's `v*.*.*` tag triggers both publish and release.
2. **Environment `crates-io`:** at least one required reviewer, "Prevent self-review" on, and a deployment policy allowing tags `v*.*.*` only.
3. **Environment `release`:** same reviewers and the same tag policy. Until 2 and 3 are configured, GitHub creates both environments on first use with no protection rules, so this PR changes nothing about who can release in the meantime.
4. **crates.io Trusted Publishing:** for `vgi-core`, `verify-trust` and `did-git-sign`, set the environment on the existing publisher (repository `OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure`, workflow `publish.yml`) to `crates-io`. Tokens requested from any other job or environment are then refused.
5. **Default workflow permissions:** set the repository (or organisation) default `GITHUB_TOKEN` permissions to read.
6. **Organisation, once every repository is pinned:** require actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA, and restrict allowed actions.

## Follow-ups

- **Verify attestations in the composite action.** After the first release made by this workflow, make `.github/actions/verify-trust` run `gh attestation verify "$RUNNER_TEMP/$asset" --repo OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure --signer-workflow OpenVTC/verifiable-git-infrastructure/.github/workflows/release.yml` before extracting. It is deliberately not in this PR: no existing release has attestations, so callers pinned to older `version:` values would break. The same-release `.sha256` check stays until then.
- **Default `version:`.** Consider changing the action's `version: latest` default to a pinned release, or documenting that callers must pin both the action ref and `version`.
- **zizmor.** Add it as a required check so pins, permissions and cache use stay this way between Dependabot updates.

## Note

The open `did-git-sign` signing-policy PR also edits the `test` job in `ci.yml`, adding steps after `cargo test --workspace`. The two changes touch separate lines and merge without conflict, but whichever lands second should be rebased so its new steps sit in the pinned, rustup-based job.

title: fix(security): compile the signing-policy bypass out and describe the gate honestly
body:
## Summary

- **Bypass variable compiled out.** `DID_GIT_SIGN_BYPASS_POLICY` no longer exists in normal builds. It is behind a non-default, test-only cargo feature that cannot be compiled into a release profile.
- **Honest docs.** The did-git-sign docs now describe the parent-process gate as what it is: a guard against accidental and naive use, not a boundary against code running as the user.
- **Namespace restriction.** `-Y sign` now refuses every sshsig namespace except `git`.
- **Testable gate.** The decision is a pure function, so its rules are tested without mutating the process environment.

## Changes

### Policy bypass (`crates/did-git-sign`)

- **New feature.** `Cargo.toml` adds a non-default feature, `insecure-policy-bypass = []`.
- **`policy.rs`:**
  - `compile_error!` when `insecure-policy-bypass` is enabled without `debug_assertions`.
  - The `BYPASS_ENV` constant exists only with the feature.
  - `bypass_requested()` is a constant `false` without the feature. With the feature, it reads the variable and prints a warning on stderr whenever the bypass is used.
  - `AuditEntry.bypass` is kept so the audit log format is unchanged. Only a feature build can set it.
- **`sign.rs`:** the refusal message no longer tells callers how to override the policy.
- **Usage check.** `grep -r DID_GIT_SIGN_BYPASS_POLICY` across local clones of this repo, openvtc, verifiable-trust-infrastructure and cierge found no users outside this crate. openvtc's only historical reference was the vendored copy of did-git-sign it removed in #159.

### Security model documentation

- **`policy.rs` module doc**, rewritten:
  - **What the gate does:** refuses unless git or `ssh-keygen` is the parent, and records every attempt.
  - **What it cannot do:** code running as the user can run real git with did-git-sign as its signing program, read the VTA credential from the keyring, or edit the audit log.
  - **What protects the key:** the VTA credential in the OS keyring.
- **`README.md`:** the "Security Model" section gains "What protects the signing key" and "The signing gate is an accident guard, not a boundary". It also states that the release binary has no bypass switch. The existing bullets move under "Other properties".

### Gate changes

- **`sign.rs` `check_namespace`:** `handle_sign` refuses any namespace other than `vgi_core::GIT_SSHSIG_NAMESPACE` (`git`). The check runs before the buffer is read or the VTA is contacted. git signs commits, tags and push certificates in `git`, so git is unaffected. The code labels this as friction, not a boundary.
- **`policy.rs` `decide(bypass, parent) -> bool`:** a pure function of the bypass flag and the raw parent name (first word, lowercased, matched by `parent_is_allowed`). `evaluate` now just gathers the inputs and calls it.

### Tests and CI

- **`policy` unit tests:**
  - `decide` admits `git`, `Git.EXE`, `git-remote-https`, `ssh-keygen`, `git --no-pager`;
  - `decide` refuses `cargo`, `gitleaks`, empty, whitespace and unknown parents;
  - only a bypass admits an unknown parent;
  - a normal build never requests a bypass;
  - the existing env-bypass test is gated on the feature and `#[serial]`.
- **`sign` unit tests:**
  - only `git` passes `check_namespace` (`file`, `email`, `""`, `Git`, `"git "`, `"git\0"` are refused);
  - `handle_sign` with namespace `file` and nonexistent paths fails with the namespace error, which shows nothing was read first.
- **`tests/policy_bypass.rs`** (new, `serial_test`):
  - a normal build with the variable set to `1`/`true`/`TRUE` still refuses a non-git parent and records `bypass: false`;
  - a feature build honours the variable and records it;
  - the default gate refuses a non-git parent.

  These tests assume the test process's parent is not git, which holds under cargo and nextest.
- **`ci.yml` `test` job**, two new steps:
  - `cargo test -p did-git-sign --features insecure-policy-bypass`;
  - `cargo build --release --locked -p did-git-sign`, failing if `target/release/did-git-sign` contains the string `DID_GIT_SIGN_BYPASS_POLICY`.

## Verification (local, rustc/cargo 1.98.1, macOS)

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | exit 0 |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | exit 0, no warnings |
| `cargo clippy -p did-git-sign --all-targets --features insecure-policy-bypass -- -D warnings` | exit 0, no warnings |
| `cargo test --workspace` | exit 0, 144 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo test -p did-git-sign --features insecure-policy-bypass` (debug) | exit 0, 73 passed, 0 failed |
| `cargo build --release --locked -p did-git-sign` | exit 0; `grep -a -c DID_GIT_SIGN_BYPASS_POLICY` on the binary: 0 |
| `cargo build -p did-git-sign --features insecure-policy-bypass` (debug) | exit 0; the same grep on the binary: 1, so the CI check detects the name when it is present |
| `cargo build --release -p did-git-sign --features insecure-policy-bypass` | exit 101: `error: the did-git-sign 'insecure-policy-bypass' feature is for debug test builds only and must not be enabled in a release build` at `policy.rs:45` |
| `ci.yml` | parses with `python3` / PyYAML |

## Compatibility

- **Default builds:** the bypass is gone, and signing refuses namespaces other than `git`. git always passes `-n git`, so normal commit, tag and push signing is unaffected.
- **Library consumers (openvtc):** no API removed. `decide` and `check_namespace` are private.
- **`--all-features`:** in a debug profile it enables the bypass for tests. In a release profile it fails to compile, by design.

## Not in this PR: moving signing into the VTA

This PR makes the gate honest and removes the free pass. It does not change what code running as the user can obtain. That needs the follow-up:

- did-git-sign asks the VTA to sign the sshsig preimage (`VtaClient::sign`) instead of fetching the Ed25519 seed;
- the did-git-sign credential is provisioned with sign-only access to its one key (no secret export);
- every signature is recorded in the VTA's own audit log.

Signing then becomes revocable, server-audited and rate-limitable, and the seed never reaches the client.

## Note

The open release-pipeline PR also edits `ci.yml`: it pins actions, replaces the toolchain action with rustup and sets read-only permissions. The two edit different lines of the `test` job and merge cleanly. The steps added here use only `run:`.

title: chore(deps): take vta-sdk 0.36 and affinidi-tdk 0.14
body:
Moves `did-git-sign` / `vgi-core` / `verify-trust` onto the **vta-sdk 0.36** line.

## Why now

OpenVTC is moving to 0.36 for peer identity vetting. The design is OpenVTC/openvtc#292; the SDK side is OpenVTC/verifiable-trust-infrastructure#1425 onward. `vta-service` 0.25.1, the MockVta OpenVTC's tests boot, already requires `^0.36`.

`did-git-sign` 0.4.8 asking for `^0.35` is exactly the edge the manifest note warns about: it would put a second `vta-sdk` in OpenVTC's binary. Nothing in this workspace needs 0.36, so the bump only moves the ceiling. `affinidi-tdk` goes to 0.14 because that is what vta-sdk 0.36 declares.

## The one deliberate compromise

This splits `trust-tasks-rs` **within this workspace**, into 0.19.4 through `trql-client` 0.17 and 0.20.3 for everything else. The registry hasn't released on 0.20 yet.

That is the bounded form the `trql-client` note already describes:
- `verify-trust` passes no trust-tasks type across the `trql-client` boundary;
- `did-git-sign`, the crate OpenVTC consumes, has no `trql-client` edge, so OpenVTC's graph still resolves **one** `trust-tasks-rs` and **one** `vta-sdk`.

The split closes when the registry releases on 0.20. The reasoning is recorded in the manifest.

## Checks

- `cargo tree -i vta-sdk -e normal,build,dev`: a single `vta-sdk v0.36.0`
- `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`: all green (65 + 30 + 26 + 14 + 1)
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

## Release

OpenVTC patches `did-git-sign` to this branch until a release carries it. The OpenVTC patch leaves when this publishes.

title: fix(jcs): bound canonicalization depth and input size
body:
fix(jcs): bound canonicalization depth and input size

jcsCanonicalize recursed once per nesting level, so canonicalizing an
attacker-influenced confirm/response threw RangeError: Maximum call stack size
exceeded. Measured on node 26: a JSON array nested 3275 levels deep (~6.5 KB of
input) is enough, and nested objects overflow at 2489 levels (~15 KB). The
document is canonicalized during verifyConfirmResponse, before anything about
it has been authenticated, so any caller of the verifier could be made to throw
an untyped error out of its request handler.

- Carry a depth counter through the encoder and reject input nesting deeper
  than JCS_MAX_DEPTH (100) — two orders of magnitude above the ~4 levels a
  Trust-Task document uses, and far below the engine's stack limit.
- Charge canonical bytes against JCS_MAX_BYTES (1 MiB) as they are emitted, so
  an oversized input fails part-way instead of being fully built. Multi-byte
  characters are counted as UTF-8 bytes.
- Both bounds are per-call overridable: jcsCanonicalize(value, { maxDepth,
  maxBytes }). Rejections throw the typed, exported JcsLimitExceededError.
- verifyDataIntegrityProof re-raises a bound violation as
  ConfirmVerificationError with the new document_too_complex reason, so callers
  catching verification failures need no special case.

Canonical output is unchanged for every in-spec document: the accounting only
counts the bytes the encoder already emitted, and the cross-implementation
fixture signed by the wallet still verifies.

Tests: 44 pass (was 35). New test/jcs.test.ts asserts a ~10 KB deeply nested
input yields JcsLimitExceededError and not a RangeError, covers the byte bound
and UTF-8 counting, and re-asserts RFC 8785 output; test/confirm.test.ts drives
the same payload through verifyConfirmResponse.

title: Require confirmation for pairing, validate the push gateway URL, re-enable ATS
body:
### Summary

This tightens how the app decides who it trusts and where it sends its push token.

- **Pairing now needs confirmation.** Scanning a pairing code or saving the VTA in Settings no longer applies the change straight away. A confirmation sheet comes first.
- **The push gateway URL is validated**, and the gateway request no longer follows redirects.
- **App Transport Security is back at its defaults** in every configuration.
- **Sign-ins are no longer auto-approved unless you turn it on.** A new "Auto-approve sign-ins" setting controls this, and it never applies in the background.
- **The APNs token is no longer logged.**

Four commits, one per change. Each can be reviewed or reverted on its own, except that the pairing commit uses the gateway URL policy from the first commit.

### Behaviour changes

**1. Push gateway URL validation and ATS** (`fix: validate the push gateway URL and refuse redirects`)
- New `GatewayURLPolicy` in the package. It requires:
  - https;
  - no userinfo, query or fragment;
  - port absent or 443;
  - a DNS host name.
- The following hosts are refused:
  - IP literals in any spelling, including decimal, hex, octal and shorthand IPv4, and IPv6;
  - single-label names;
  - local-only suffixes (`localhost`, `.local`, `.internal`, `.lan`, `.arpa`, `.svc`, …).
- A host outside the paired VTA's `did:web`/`did:webvh` domain is a **warning** (`hostNotBoundToVta`), shown in Settings and on the pairing sheet. It is not a refusal.
- The URL is checked when it is written (pairing, Settings) and again before the POST.
- `GatewayClient` takes an injectable `URLSession`. The default session is ephemeral, has a 15 s timeout, and keeps no cookies, cache or credentials. Redirects are refused, both on the session and per task.
- `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads` is removed from `project.yml`. No local-networking exception was added, because the VTA and mediator are reached by the engine, not `URLSession`.
- `ios-app-build` now fails if any `NSAllowsArbitraryLoads*` key appears in the generated `Info.plist`.

**2. Pairing review and confirmation** (`feat: review and confirm pairings before applying them`)
- `PairingPayload.parse` accepts only `cierge-pair://`. The raw-JSON form is removed.
- New `PairingPolicy` in the package:
  - The mediator is taken from the VTA's DID document. A mediator in the code is only cross-checked, and a mismatch is refused.
  - A DID document with no mediator is refused.
  - The gateway must pass `GatewayURLPolicy`.
- `AgentModel.applyPairing` is replaced by two steps:
  - `stagePairing` resolves the DID document, runs the policy and shows `PairingConfirmSheet`. It saves nothing and does not connect.
  - `confirmPairing` applies the change.
- When the pairing replaces a **different** VTA, `confirmPairing`:
  - requires device-owner authentication (biometrics or passcode, via an injectable `DeviceOwnerAuthenticator`);
  - disconnects;
  - discards pending approvals and task consents;
  - turns push wake off;
  - then saves and connects.
- The sheet shows the VTA DID with its verified name, the domain, the mediator, the gateway host and the stated tenant. A red banner appears when the pairing replaces a different VTA.
- Settings no longer saves on every keystroke. VTA DID and gateway edits are drafts until **Save**, which goes through the same review. The mediator field is now read-only.
- Removed `resolveFromDid` and `saveConfig`.
- Added `NSFaceIDUsageDescription`.

**3. Sign-in auto-approve setting** (`feat: ask before approving sign-ins; never approve in the background`)
- New `StepUpPolicy.decide` in the package. A step-up is auto-approved only if all three hold:
  - it has no authorization context;
  - the app is active;
  - **Settings → Behaviour → Auto-approve sign-ins** is on.
- Everything else is queued for Approve/Deny with a notification.
- A background push wake always passes `appActive: false`, so it only queues.

**4. APNs token logging** (`fix: stop logging the APNs device token`)
- The token `print` is removed.
- The Test tab's token row is DEBUG-only and shows an 8-character prefix.
- Engine log directives are `warn` in non-DEBUG builds.

### Product decisions to confirm

- **"Auto-approve sign-ins" defaults to off.** Existing users will be asked to approve every sign-in until they turn it on.
- **Re-pairing to a different VTA requires device-owner authentication.** A device with no passcode set cannot replace its VTA.
- **The gateway domain check is a warning, not a block.** Gateways run by a different domain than the VTA remain possible after the operator sees the warning.
- **A VTA whose DID document advertises no `#vta-didcomm` mediator can no longer be paired.** Manual mediator entry is gone.
- **The Test tab no longer shows or copies the full APNs token.**

### Upgrade notes

- Existing pairings are not re-prompted.
- A previously saved gateway URL that breaks a hard rule, such as `http://` or an IP address, is refused when push is registered, with a message in the Test tab. Re-save it in Settings.

### Not in this PR

- Signed pairing offers and nonce-bound enrolment.
- DID-addressed push gateway.
- Keychain accessibility changes for the holder key.
- Push-wake rate limiting.

### Testing

- **New package tests** (iOS Simulator, `VtaMobileAgent-Package`):
  - `GatewayURLPolicyTests`
  - `GatewayClientTests` (a `URLProtocol` stub answering 307)
  - `PairingPolicyTests`
  - `StepUpPolicyTests`
  - one new case in `StepUpTests`
  - `testParsesRawJson` replaced by `testRejectsRawJson`
- **App-target logic is not unit-tested.** `stagePairing`, `confirmPairing` and the `appActive` wiring are kept as thin glue around the package policies, because the app target has no test bundle.
- **Pre-CI checks** (a host without Xcode):
  - The pure package files and their tests were built and run on macOS with an XCTest stand-in: 41 tests, 0 failures.
  - The full package, all test files and the app target were typechecked for Mac Catalyst against the `vta-mobile-core-v0.6.17` headers, with no errors. `PairingScanner` was stubbed there because VisionKit is unavailable on Catalyst.
  - `xcodegen generate` plus the new ATS check were verified in both directions.
- **Still needs CI and a device:**
  - `xcodebuild test` on the simulator;
  - the app build;
  - on a device: QR pairing, the re-pair Face ID/passcode prompt, the Settings Save flow, and push wake queuing a sign-in.

title: feat(vetting): guided join, vetter directory and profile, QR tickets, grant checks, resend and branding (#302) (#307)
body:
feat(vetting): guided join, vetter directory and profile, QR tickets, grant checks, resend and branding (#302) (#307)

* chore(deps): move the VTI patches to the vetter registry commit on VTI main

The vetter directory, profile, resend, branding and ticket links need the VTI vetter registry work, which merged as 14ef89a on VTI main (#1430). Pin every VTI patch to that commit; the branch they used to name no longer exists.



* feat(vetting): the vetter registry, ticket links and grant revocation checks in core

A vetting community can now be found, and its vetters found and checked, from
openvtc-core:

- queries: questions put to a community (manifest, vetter directory, vetter
  profile, grant resend) are remembered in memory by document id, so an
  answer — or a trust-task-error — is claimed only when it answers something
  we asked. Anything else still reaches the join handler. Unanswered
  questions expire after 30 s (R1.2), and refusals read as sentences a person
  can act on (notEligible, notGranted, permissionDenied, malformedRequest).
- registry: typed forms for the vetter profile, its events and the directory
  filters become the SDK bodies and are checked with its check_shape before
  anything is sent. The last profile sent is kept in the book as JSON, so an
  older build still opens a config a newer one wrote.
- inbound: list, profile and resend responses and refusals; a manifest now
  answers whoever asked and teaches the community's branding. A verified
  eligibility presentation whose grant names a status list hands back a
  GrantCheck for the caller to run.
- status: that check, with an https-only, timeout-bounded fetch whose errors
  tell an unreachable host from an HTTP error from a body that is not a
  status list (R6.4).
- book: known communities with their branding (so "does not vet" is told
  apart from "never asked"), requirements already known adopted by a new
  application, and the memberships that can ask for their grant again.
- applicant: the grant's revocation status per request, a pasted ticket link
  read and refused when it is for another community, and the next step.
- guide: a community's requirements in plain words.
- tickets: a ticket as a vetting-ticket: link carrying the scanned form.



* feat(vetting): a guided join, the vetter directory and profile, QR tickets and grant checks

The TUI side of the vetter registry (VTI #1430).

Guided join. After the community's DID, the join flow decides from what the book
knows whether the community vets. If it does, the page says what it requires in
plain words, shows this persona's application with its next step, and offers
three ways on: start or continue the application (choosing persona and context,
then opening the Vetting page on it), join anyway (the community refers it), or
cancel. An application that meets the requirements joins as its persona and
says its statements go with the request.

When the book does not know, the community is asked. The join flow cannot hear
the answer: its loop selects only on actions and interrupts, and inbound
messages are read by the runtime loop's arm, which is parked while the flow
runs. So the flow sends manifest/0.2 (the send bounded at 15 s) and returns
JoinExit::AwaitRequirements. The runtime loop keeps the join screen up, keeps
reading inbound messages, and enters the flow again on the manifest, a
refusal or an unreadable answer, or after 15 s. Nothing waits without a
deadline. The degraded loop has no inbound arm and uses the book only.

Vetting page:
- Find vetters (v): filters for language, place, method, event dates and name,
  paged by cursor. Results stay in page state; ask this vetter fills the
  request form and says a ticket is still needed, quoting their contact hint.
- Your vetter profile (p on Tickets): listed or not, name, languages, location,
  methods, documentation (from VetterPolicy), availability, contact hint and
  events (add, edit, remove), checked with check_shape before sending. The
  community's answer or notEligible is shown and kept.
- Tickets are shown as a QR code of their vetting-ticket: link, in Unicode
  half-blocks sized to the window; u copies the link. A pasted link fills the
  request form and is refused for another community.
- A vetter's verified grant is checked for revocation in the background and
  shown as named until …, revoked, or could not check.
- g asks a community to resend a vetter credential; notGranted is said plainly.
- Community branding: an accent swatch beside the name here and on the
  Communities panel, in the literal colour, and the published name as a
  fallback.

qrcode 0.14 is added without default features: MIT OR Apache-2.0 with no
dependencies of its own, so deny.toml needs nothing.



* docs(vetting): as-built notes for the vetter registry, ticket links, guided join, grant checks, resend and branding

Adds as-built notes to vetting-process.md where each feature departs from or
fills in the text: the registry and profile (§7), the revocation check
(§7.1), ticket links and QR codes (§8.2), resend (§10.3), the guided join path
and why the wait for a manifest lives in the runtime loop (§12.3), and branding
(§6.1). Decisions D25–D29 record the choices.



* fix(vetting): keep the grant check's future Send

The revocation check is spawned by the TUI, so its future has to be Send. The
status fetch borrowed the client and the status list URL across its await,
which is not provably Send for every lifetime the SDK's AsyncFn(&str) may be
called with. The fetch now takes a cloned client and an owned URL, and a test
asserts the future is Send, so a regression fails in core rather than in a
spawn site.



* docs(deps): say why the VTI patches pin a rev on VTI main

The patch comment still described a feature-branch pin. Describe the rev pin on VTI main instead, and when the entries go.

title: fix(config): release builds ignore VTA and mediator environment overrides
body:
## Summary

`OPENVTC_VTA_URL`, `OPENVTC_VTA_DID` and `OPENVTC_MEDIATOR_DID` choose which VTA
and mediator OpenVTC authenticates to. Until now any build applied them without
validation or a visible indication, and the next save wrote them into the
profile:

- the VTA URL/DID reached `SecuredConfig`;
- the mediator went through `set_active_mediator_did` into the account record.

So a variable set for one launch stayed in effect after it was unset.

This PR makes them a development-only seam.

## Behaviour change

**Release builds (default features)**

- The three variables are never applied.
- Each one that is set is reported:
  - one line on stderr before the TUI starts: `OPENVTC_VTA_URL is set but ignored: release builds do not accept trust-anchor overrides.`;
  - the same message in the Activity Log.
- The setup wizard's `OPENVTC_VTA_URL` shortcut is gated the same way. The enter-DID page shows the warning and resolves the DID as normal.
- `OPENVTC_FRIENDLY_NAME` is cosmetic and still honoured.

**`dev-overrides` builds** (new cargo feature on `openvtc`, off by default)

- Values are validated:
  - `OPENVTC_VTA_DID` and `OPENVTC_MEDIATOR_DID` must parse as a DID;
  - `OPENVTC_VTA_URL` must be an `http://` or `https://` URL with a host.
  - A value that fails validation is ignored and logged.
- Overrides apply to the running process only:
  - the VTA URL/DID are replaced in memory, and the displaced values are kept in a new runtime-only `Config::runtime_trust_overrides`;
  - `Config::save`, `Config::export` and `Config::clone_for_save` write the stored originals (`SecuredConfig::from` and `Config::key_backend_for_save`);
  - the mediator override uses the new `Config::set_active_mediator_did_runtime`, which updates the runtime identity and never the account record.
- While any override is active, a red `DEV OVERRIDE: VTA → <url> · …` badge stays at the front of the main page's bottom bar. A startup line on stderr and an Activity Log entry also record it.

## Migration for developers

If you point a local build at a development VTA or mediator through these
variables, add the feature:

```bash
OPENVTC_VTA_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8080 cargo run -p openvtc --features dev-overrides
```

A binary built without the feature, including `cargo install`, release
artifacts and plain `cargo run`, now ignores the variables.

Usage search:

- In this repo, nothing but the code changed here reads them. Scripts,
  workflows and tests don't use them. `openvtc-core/tests/mockvta_bootstrap_e2e.rs`
  calls the URL-direct SDK function and never sets `OPENVTC_VTA_URL`.
- In `vti-setup`, `verifiable-trust-infrastructure`, `cierge` and `dtg-demo`
  there are no references, so no runbook or script depends on them with a
  release binary.

## Implementation

- `openvtc/src/env_overrides.rs` (new) contains the override logic, moved out of `main.rs`.
  - `apply_from(config, env_fn) -> OverrideReport { applied, ignored }` takes the environment as a closure.
  - `apply_env_overrides(config)` calls `apply_from` with the process environment.
  - Also here: the wizard URL gate, the pre-TUI notice, and `surface()`, which writes the report to the Activity Log and sets the badge.
- `openvtc-core`:
  - `Config::runtime_trust_overrides` / `OriginalTrustAnchors`;
  - `override_vta_url_runtime`, `override_vta_did_runtime`, `set_active_mediator_did_runtime`, `persisted_vta_anchor`, `key_backend_for_save`;
  - `SecuredConfig::from(&Config)` writes the persisted anchor.
- Both call sites in `state_handler/mod.rs` (post-setup and normal load) consume the report.
- The stderr line is printed in `main.rs` just before the TUI starts. The call sites run after the TUI has taken the terminal, where a stderr write would corrupt the screen.
- CI: a new `Test (dev-overrides)` job runs `cargo clippy -p openvtc --all-targets --features dev-overrides -- -D warnings` and `cargo test -p openvtc --features dev-overrides`.
- Docs: `openvtc/README.md` (feature flag table and a "Developer trust-anchor overrides" section), `openvtc-core/README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and related doc comments.

`Config` gains a public field, so external code building `Config` with a
struct literal must add `runtime_trust_overrides: None`.

## Tests

All tests use an injected environment closure; none mutate the process
environment.

- Release builds:
  - `release_build_ignores_trust_anchor_env`
  - `release_build_still_honours_the_friendly_name`
  - `release_build_startup_notice_says_the_variables_are_ignored`
  - `release_build_wizard_ignores_the_url_override`
- `dev-overrides` builds:
  - `dev_build_applies_but_does_not_persist`: runtime values change; the `clone_for_save` snapshot and `SecuredConfig::from` of the live config keep the stored URL/DID.
  - `dev_build_rejects_values_that_do_not_validate`
  - `dev_build_wizard_validates_the_url_override`
- Both builds:
  - `mediator_env_override_never_touches_account_record`
  - `blank_values_read_as_unset`
  - `surfacing_logs_ignored_and_pins_the_banner`
- `openvtc-core`:
  - `runtime_mediator_override_leaves_the_account_record_alone`
  - `runtime_vta_override_is_never_what_a_save_writes`

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --features openvtc/dev-overrides -- -D warnings`
- `cargo test -p openvtc-core -p openvtc`
- `cargo test -p openvtc-core -p openvtc --features dev-overrides`

## Not in this PR

- `OPENVTC_CONFIG_PATH` and `OPENVTC_CONFIG_PROFILE` are unchanged.
- The wizard's "Warning:" line uses `MessageType::Info`. Adding a warning variant would touch every setup page renderer.

title: fix(config): release builds ignore VTA and mediator environment overrides (#305)
body:
fix(config): release builds ignore VTA and mediator environment overrides (#305)

OPENVTC_VTA_URL, OPENVTC_VTA_DID and OPENVTC_MEDIATOR_DID choose which VTA
and mediator this client authenticates to. Any build applied them unvalidated
and silently, and the next save persisted them: the VTA URL/DID through
SecuredConfig, the mediator through set_active_mediator_did into the account
record. One launch with the variables set therefore changed the profile.

They are now honoured only by a build with the new dev-overrides feature on
the openvtc crate (off by default). Without it every set variable is ignored
and reported, once on stderr before the TUI starts and again in the Activity
Log. The setup wizard's own OPENVTC_VTA_URL shortcut goes through the same
gate. OPENVTC_FRIENDLY_NAME is cosmetic and still honoured.

In a dev-overrides build the values are validated (DIDs must parse, the URL
must be http(s) with a host) and applied to the running process only. The
displaced VTA URL/DID are held in Config::runtime_trust_overrides, and
SecuredConfig::from and clone_for_save write those originals back. The
mediator goes through set_active_mediator_did_runtime, which never touches
the account record. A DEV OVERRIDE badge holds the bottom bar while any
override is active.

The override logic moves from main.rs into env_overrides.rs behind an
injectable environment closure, so the tests never mutate process env. CI
gains a job that runs clippy and tests for openvtc with dev-overrides.

title: ci: pin every action to a commit SHA, and drop the write-scoped token
body:
ci: pin every action to a commit SHA, and drop the write-scoped token

The plugin is installed by cloning main, and hooks.json runs the plugin
binary at every SessionStart, so whatever can write to main runs code on
every installing machine. Two things made that reachable from CI: every
third-party action was a mutable ref (actions/checkout@v4,
Swatinem/rust-cache@v2, and dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable, which is a
branch), and the workflow declared no permissions block at all, so it
inherited the repository default token - which is write.

Every uses: is now a full 40-character commit SHA with the release it
corresponds to in a trailing comment:

  actions/checkout     34e114876b0b11c390a56381ad16ebd13914f8d5  v4.3.1
  Swatinem/rust-cache  6323deb102c322ba6fcbdcafc7e3dddab59af2b6  v2.9.2

The rust-cache SHA is the commit the annotated v2.9.2 tag points at, not
the tag object.

dtolnay/rust-toolchain is gone rather than pinned. It derives the
toolchain from the ref name, so pinning the branch by SHA would have
quietly frozen which toolchain CI installs. Hosted runners ship rustup,
so Install Rust is a run: step with an explicit version, and that version
lives in one place (RUST_TOOLCHAIN) with a check that Cargo.toml's
rust-version agrees. The toolchain the README promises is now the one CI
actually builds with, and a drift between the two fails the job instead
of going unnoticed.

Least privilege, because none of this workflow pushes, comments or
publishes: permissions: contents: read at the top level, and
persist-credentials: false on all three checkouts so the token is not
left behind in .git/config. The cache is written only from main, so a
pull request can read it but cannot seed what later runs restore.

A new "workflow hygiene" job keeps it that way: it fails on any uses: that
is not a 40-hex SHA (local ./ actions exempt, a docker:// image must be
pinned by digest) and on any workflow without a top-level permissions
block. Pinning that nothing enforces lasts until the next person adds a
step.

dependabot.yml covers github-actions and cargo, weekly. Dependabot
rewrites a SHA pin and its version comment together, so pinning is not
freezing. cooldown holds a release back for seven days before proposing
it: a hijacked or re-tagged release is usually noticed and pulled within
days, and this keeps it from arriving as a routine bump on day one.
Security updates are not delayed by it.

Two things still need a repository admin, and they are what make the
pinning matter: set the default workflow permissions to read-only, and
protect main so a write token cannot push to it directly.

title: fix(health): probe only public HTTPS transport endpoints, and never follow a redirect
body:
## Summary

`openvtc health` probes the transport URLs published in each resolved DID document. Those URLs come from documents anyone can publish, and the probe client dialled them as written: any scheme the filter let through, any host, the system proxy, and up to 10 redirects. Resolution itself was already guarded by `affinidi-did-web`, but that guard lives on the resolver's own HTTP client and never reached the probe.

The probe now applies the same policy:

- **Probe client** (`probe_client`): redirects disabled (a 3xx still counts as reachable), no proxy, a connect timeout, and, by default, `affinidi_did_web::guarded_dns_resolver()`. That resolver refuses a hostname that resolves to a non-routable address and connects only to the addresses it checked.
- **URL vetting before any I/O** (`vet_probe_url`). The DNS guard never sees IP-literal hosts, so the parsed URL is checked first. It refuses:
  - an unparseable URL;
  - a non-HTTPS scheme (plaintext endpoints are listed, not dialled);
  - userinfo;
  - a loopback, private, CGNAT, link-local or `localhost`/`.local` host, checked after WHATWG canonicalisation.

  The parsed URL that was vetted is the one sent.
- **New `Probe::Blocked { url, reason }`** (`"status": "blocked"` in `--json`, additive). `grade()` returns `None` for it. It adds a finding line, and a DNS-guard refusal found in the error chain also maps to it. `is_healthy` is unchanged: a blocked endpoint is reported, not treated as a broken chain.
- **`--allow-private-probes`** on `health` restores plaintext and private-address probing for local development stacks, and prints a one-line warning when used. Userinfo and non-HTTP schemes are still refused. `build_report` stays public-only; `build_report_with_progress` now takes a `ProbePolicy`.

The host classifier is a local copy of `affinidi-did-web` 0.1.4's (`openvtc-core/src/net_guard.rs`), with that crate's test vectors. It is marked to be replaced by the exported API once `affinidi-did-web` publishes one. `affinidi-did-web` becomes a direct dependency at the version already in `Cargo.lock`, so there is no new crate and no version change (the lockfile diff is one line).

## Breaking change (library API)

`openvtc_core::health::build_report_with_progress` gains a `policy: ProbePolicy` argument, and `Probe` gains a variant. The only in-tree caller is `openvtc/src/health_cmd.rs`, which is updated.

## Tests

New in `openvtc-core/src/health.rs`:

- `probe_refuses_loopback_literal_without_dialing`: a loopback listener sees no connection.
- `probe_refuses_plain_http`
- `probe_client_dns_guard_refuses_localhost_name`: the DNS guard is installed and its refusal is recognised in the error chain.
- `probe_does_not_follow_redirects`: the redirect target receives no request.
- `health_report_blocks_did_peer_inline_internal_service`: end to end through `build_report`, for both plaintext and HTTPS forms.
- `probe_urls_are_vetted_after_canonicalisation`: alternate IP encodings, IPv6 forms, names, userinfo, schemes.
- `allow_private_admits_dev_endpoints_but_not_credentials`
- `a_blocked_probe_is_a_finding_but_not_a_fault`: JSON shape, finding line, health unchanged.

New in `openvtc-core/src/net_guard.rs`: the classifier vectors from `affinidi-did-web`.

title: refactor(vta-sdk)!: vetting wire types come from the published trust-tasks specs
body:
## Why

The peer identity vetting Trust Tasks are specified in trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf, and `trust-tasks-codegen` generates Rust types for every one of them, published in `trust-tasks-rs` 0.20.4 under `trust_tasks_rs::specs`. The vetting stack (#1425–#1432) hand-wrote copies of those types instead — mainly `vta-sdk/src/protocols/vetting.rs`, ~2,450 lines and 39 public types — used by `vtc-service`, `vtc-client` and `cnm-cli`. The copies had already drifted from the specifications: a documented shape the schema refused, and an admin console calling a Trust Task URI that no route bound.

This makes the generated types the vetting wire layer. Nothing restates them, and a guard stops the next copy being written.

## What is generated, and what is still hand-written

**Generated, re-exported by `vta-sdk`:**

| Task | Where |
|---|---|
| `vetting/request/0.1` | `vta_sdk::protocols::vetting::request::v0_1` |
| `vetting/session/0.1` (with the Vetting Card) | `vta_sdk::protocols::vetting::session::v0_1` |
| `vetting/decline/0.1` | `vta_sdk::protocols::vetting::decline::v0_1` |
| `vtc/vetting/revoke-statement/0.1` | `vta_sdk::protocols::vetting::revoke_statement::v0_1` |
| `vtc/vetting/vetters/{grant,profile,list,resend}/0.1` | `vta_sdk::protocols::vetting::vetters::{grant,profile,list,resend}::v0_1` |
| `vtc/join-requests/manifest/{0.1,0.2}` | `vta_sdk::protocols::join_requests::manifest::{v0_1,v0_2}` |
| Requirements vocabulary (`VettingRequirements`, `VettingMethod`, `VettingRelationship`, `VettingDocumentation`, `ClaimType`) | `vta_sdk::protocols::vetting`, re-exported from manifest 0.2 |

Type URI constants (`VETTING_*_TYPE`, `JOIN_REQUEST_MANIFEST_*`) are the generated types' `TYPE_URI`.

**Hand-written, operating on the generated types:**

- `CheckShape` / `read_checked` (+ `read_request`, `read_requirements`, `read_branding`): validates against the schema each generated type embeds — read from the JSON **as received**, because some generated constructors normalise what they parse (a date written `2026-1-05` parses as `2026-01-05`) — then applies the rules the schema validator does not check: an event's `endDate` ≥ `startDate` and span ≤ 31 days, `eventTo` ≥ `eventFrom`, every `minByMethod` method in `acceptedMethods`, `joinDid` = document issuer — and `format: uri`. The schemas give an event's `url`, branding's `logoUrl` and the requirements' `governanceFrameworkUrl` `format: uri` with `^https://` and ≤ 2048, but the validator treats `format` as an annotation and does not assert it, so the layer enforces it by hand: an absolute https URI (RFC 3986) with a host, no whitespace or control characters. It runs on profile publish, listing responses, and branding PUT and storage, which refuse such a value; the admin console applies the same rule. Manifest 0.2 emission does not fail over branding: if stored branding breaks the rule (only a row written before the check could), the manifest is served without `branding` and a warning names the member at fault, not its value — branding is presentation only, and the manifest is what every applicant needs to join.
- `IdentityVettingEndorsement`, the Vetting Statement's credential body. It is `vetting/_shared/0.1/identity-vetting`, which is not a Trust Task, and the codegen does not generate shared definitions; its members now use the generated vocabulary types.
- Card and statement signing and verification, eligibility VP verification (`vetting/eligibility.rs`), credential status checks (`status.rs`), match codes, ticket URIs, requirements evaluation and digest.
- Extended error code constants (the codegen emits none).
- Admin REST bodies that are not Trust Tasks: `VetterGrantRow`/`VetterGrantListResponse` (`GET /v1/vetting/vetters`), `AutoGrantConfig`/`AutoGrantStatus` (`/v1/vetting/auto-grant`), `VettingRevocationRow` (`/v1/vetting/revocations`).

**REST routes that carry a task's body now take and return the generated types:** `POST /v1/vetting/vetters` (grant), `POST /v1/vetting/vetters/{memberDid}/resend`, `POST /v1/vetting/vetters/list`, `GET /v1/join-requests/manifest` (admin 0.2 and public 0.1). `GET`/`PUT /v1/community/branding` keeps its own route but its body *is* the manifest 0.2 `CommunityBranding` definition, so it takes the generated type rather than a copy — what an admin stores is exactly what the manifest publishes.

**OpenAPI.** Generated types are foreign, so `ToSchema` cannot be derived on them. The new `vta_sdk::openapi` module (feature `openapi`) provides transparent wrappers (`VetterGrant01Payload`, `JoinManifest02Response`, …) whose schemas are rendered from the JSON Schema the generated type embeds. Components are named after the specification — `VtcVettingVettersListV0_1ListedVetter` — so two specs' `VetterEvent`s cannot collide. `admin-ui/openapi.json` and `wire.ts` are regenerated; `wire-types.ts` aliases the new names, and the console's hand-written `VettingRequirements` interface is replaced by the alias. (utoipa's model has no fields for `dependentSchemas`, `dependentRequired`, `not` or `propertyNames`; those are enforced at runtime.)

## trust-tasks bump

All five crates move to **0.20.4** (`trust-tasks-rs`, `-https`, `-didcomm`, `-proof`, `-capability-client`), all published on crates.io. `Cargo.lock` updated; `check-lockfile-self-pins.sh`, `check-workspace-version-reqs.py`, `check-nitro-copies-every-member.py` and `check-authz-context-types.sh` pass. The workspace dependency already enables `validate` and `all-specs`, so no feature change was needed. `trust-tasks-rs` becomes a **required** dependency of `vta-sdk`, because the always-compiled protocol modules re-export it. No crate `version =` was edited.

## Wire divergences (the specification wins)

| Member | Before | Now | Who is affected |
|---|---|---|---|
| every `ext` | any JSON value accepted (`{}`, `{"x":1}`) | an object with ≥ 1 member whose keys are reverse-DNS namespaces (SPEC §4.5.1) | any producer of these tasks, and branding `ext` |
| `vetting/request` `introduction` | any JSON value | a JSON object; a ticket and an introduction (even `{}`) together are refused | applicants and vetters (openvtc) |
| `vetting/request` `ticket` | extra members inside `{code}` / `{ticketId, secret}` ignored | refused (`additionalProperties: false`) | applicants |
| `vetting/request` `languages` | omitted when empty | sent as `[]` when set to an empty list | applicant producers |
| `vetting/request#response` `acceptsDocumentation` | `[]` accepted, omitted when empty | `minItems: 1`, unique | vetters' clients |
| `vetting/request#response` `eligibilityVp` | any JSON value | the published `EligibilityPresentation` shape (`@context`, `type`, `holder`, `verifiableCredential`, `nonce`, `domain`, `authentication` proof) | vetters' clients |
| `vetting/session` `requiredClaims`/`optionalClaims` | any strings (portrait refused) | `ClaimType` pattern, unique, portrait refused; `optionalClaims` sent as `[]` if set empty | vetters' clients |
| Vetting Card `id` | any string | `urn:uuid:` + a UUID | applicants' clients |
| Vetting Card claim `type` | any string | `ClaimType` pattern, ≤ 128 | applicants' clients |
| Vetting Card `cardVersion` | `u32` (0 accepted) | integer ≥ 1 | none in practice (the SDK writes 1) |
| Vetting Card `proof` | optional in the type | required by the schema (verification already required it) | none |
| Statement endorsement `documentClasses` / `claimsVerified` | duplicates accepted, `none` accepted, claims any string | unique; `none` never listed (the shared definition: no document is the empty list); claims are `ClaimType` | vetters signing; the community stops counting a statement that breaks this |
| `vtc/vetting/revoke-statement` `statementDigestMultibase` | any string (the community decoded it later) | `DigestMultibase` pattern, ≥ 16 chars | vetters |
| manifest 0.2 `vetting.independence` | always emitted as `{"requireConsistentIdentityCommitment": false}` when absent | emitted only as registered | **every `requirementsDigest` of a criterion without explicit independence changes once**; applicants who recorded one mid-application see it change |
| manifest 0.2 `vetting.acceptedDocumentClasses` | `[]` accepted | `minItems: 1`, unique | community admins |
| manifest 0.2 `vetting.acceptedMethods` | duplicates accepted | unique | community admins |
| manifest 0.2 `vetting.version` | leading zeros accepted (`01.1`) | `(0\|[1-9][0-9]*)\.(0\|[1-9][0-9]*)` | community admins |
| manifest 0.2 `vetting.requiredClaims`/`optionalClaims` | any strings | `ClaimType` pattern, unique | community admins |
| manifest criterion `id` / `description` | unbounded | 1–128 / ≤ 1024 (manifest 0.2); registering a criterion the manifest cannot publish is refused | community admins |
| `vtc/vetting/vetters/list#response` `vetters` | no cap | ≤ 100 (the listing never exceeded it) | none |
| `listing` cursors | bound to the old serialisation of the filters | bound to the generated type's; a cursor issued before the upgrade is refused once | anyone paging a listing across the upgrade |
| OpenAPI component names | `VetterGrantBody`, `ListedVetter`, `CommunityBranding`, `JoinRequestManifestResponseBody`, … | spec-named (`VtcVettingVettersGrantV0_1Payload`, …) | generated OpenAPI clients (the admin console is updated) |

Unchanged on the wire: member names and casing, event dates (still exactly `YYYY-MM-DD` as received), URL members (an event `url`, `logoUrl` and `governanceFrameworkUrl` are still refused unless they are an absolute https URI of at most 2048 characters with no whitespace or control characters — the schemas' `format: uri`, which the validator does not assert, is checked by hand), grant validity bounds, listing bounds and order, admin REST status codes (still 400 for a body that breaks its schema; `malformedRequest` over Trust Tasks).

## `vta-sdk` public API changes a consumer (openvtc) must make

Generated structs are `#[non_exhaustive]`: construct with `X::builder()` + `X::try_from(builder)` or by deserializing; constrained strings are newtypes (`TryFrom<&str>`, deref to `String`). Import `vta_sdk::protocols::vetting::CheckShape` where `check_shape()` is called.

**`vta_sdk::protocols::vetting`**

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `VettingRequestBody` | `request::v0_1::Payload` |
| `TicketPresentation::Scanned { ticket_id, secret }` / `::Code { code }` | `request::v0_1::Ticket::QrTicket(QrTicket { ticket_id, secret })` / `::ShortCodeTicket(ShortCodeTicket { code })` |
| `VettingRequestAcceptedBody` | `request::v0_1::Response` |
| `VettingSessionBody` / `VettingSessionResponseBody` | `session::v0_1::Payload` / `session::v0_1::Response` |
| `VettingCard` (`types`, `proof: Option<Value>`) | `session::v0_1::VettingCard` (`type_`, `proof: DataIntegrityProof`) |
| `CardClaim { claim_type, value, provenance }` | `session::v0_1::VettingCardClaim { type_, value, provenance }` |
| `VettingDeclineBody`, `DeclineCode` | `decline::v0_1::Payload`, `decline::v0_1::PayloadCode` |
| `RevokeStatementBody`, `RevocationReason`, `RevokeStatementResponseBody` | `revoke_statement::v0_1::{Payload, PayloadReason, Response}` |
| `VetterGrantBody`, `VetterGrantResponseBody` | `vetters::grant::v0_1::{Payload, Response}` (`validity_seconds: Option<i64>`) |
| `VetterProfileBody`, `VetterProfileResponseBody`, `VetterLocation`, `VetterEvent` | `vetters::profile::v0_1::{Payload, Response, VetterLocation, VetterEvent}` |
| `VetterListBody`, `VetterListResponseBody`, `ListedVetter` | `vetters::list::v0_1::{Payload, Response, ListedVetter}` |
| `VetterListBody::has_event_filter()` | `has_event_filter(&body)` |
| `VetterResendBody`, `VetterResendResponseBody` | `vetters::resend::v0_1::{Payload, Response}` |
| `VettingRequirements`, `EligibleVetters`, `Independence`, `InvitationRequirement` | `VettingRequirements`, `VettingRequirementsEligibleVetters`, `VettingRequirementsIndependence` (members now `Option`s), `VettingRequirementsInvitation` |
| `VettingRequirements::validate()`, `InvalidRequirements` | `CheckShape::check_shape()` or `read_requirements(&json)`; `ShapeError` |
| `VettingRequirements::max_statement_age()` | `max_statement_age(&requirements)` |
| `VettingMethod::as_str()` / `::parse()` | `Display` / `FromStr` (generated enum, same path) |
| `DeclaredRelationship` | `VettingRelationship` |
| `<type>::check_shape()` (inherent) | `CheckShape::check_shape()` (trait) |
| `VettingRequestBody::check_shape(issuer)` | `check_request(&payload, issuer)` or `read_request(&json, issuer)` |
| `ShapeError::TicketAndIntroduction` (enum was `Copy`) | `ShapeError::Schema(String)`; enum no longer `Copy` |
| `IdentityVettingEndorsement` `document_classes: Vec<String>`, `claims_verified: Vec<String>`, `declared_relationship: DeclaredRelationship` | `Vec<VettingDocumentation>`, `Vec<ClaimType>`, `VettingRelationship` |
| `VETTING_CARD_TYPES: [&str; 3]` | `[session::v0_1::VettingCardTypeItem; 3]` |
| `DEFAULT_VETTER_LIST_LIMIT: u32` | `u64` |
| `MAX_VETTER_{NAME_CHARS,LANGUAGES,METHODS,ACCEPTED_DOCUMENTATION,AVAILABILITY_CHARS,CONTACT_HINT_CHARS,EVENTS,EVENT_NAME_CHARS}`, `MAX_VETTING_URL_CHARS`, `MAX_VETTER_LIST_LIMIT`, `MAX_VETTER_LIST_CURSOR_CHARS` | removed — the schemas carry these bounds |
| `VetterProfileSummary.methods: Vec<VettingMethod>` | `Vec<vetters::profile::v0_1::VettingMethod>` |
| — | new: `read_checked`, `read_request`, `read_requirements`, `read_branding`, `CheckShape`, `check_request`, `has_event_filter`, `max_statement_age`; re-exports `ClaimType`, `VettingDocumentation` |

**`vta_sdk::protocols::join_requests`** (feature `didcomm`, as before)

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `JoinRequestManifestResponseBody` | `manifest::v0_1::Response` (0.1) / `manifest::v0_2::Response` (0.2) |
| `ManifestCriterion` (`presentation_definition: Value`) | `manifest::v0_1::ResponseCriteriaItem` / `manifest::v0_2::Criterion` (`presentation_definition: serde_json::Map`) |
| `CommunityBranding`, `::is_empty()`, `::check_shape()`, `MAX_BRANDING_*` | `manifest::v0_2::CommunityBranding`; `read_branding` / `CheckShape`; bounds in the schema |

**`vta_sdk::vetting`** (feature `vetting`)

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `card::CardDraft.claims: Vec<CardClaim>`; `identity_commitment(salt, &[CardClaim], …)` | `Vec<VettingCardClaim>`; `&[VettingCardClaim]` |
| `card::VerifiedVettingCard::card() -> &VettingCard`, `::claim() -> Option<&CardClaim>` | `&session::v0_1::VettingCard`, `Option<&VettingCardClaim>` |
| card `id` any string | must be `urn:uuid:<uuid>` |
| `requirements::StatementFacts.{method, declared_relationship}`, `Evaluation.by_relationship`, `Need::Method` | the generated `VettingMethod` / `VettingRelationship` |
| `ticket_uri::TicketUri.presentation: TicketPresentation` (`TicketUri: PartialEq + Eq`) | `request::v0_1::Ticket` (no `PartialEq`/`Eq`) |
| `ticket_uri::encode() -> String` | `-> Result<String, VettingError>` |

**`vta_sdk::openapi`** (new, feature `openapi`): the documentation wrappers above.

**`vtc-client`**

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `grant_vetter(member_did, validity_seconds)` | `grant_vetter(&vetting::vetters::grant::v0_1::Payload)` |
| `VetterGrant.grant: VetterGrantResponseBody` (`VetterGrant: PartialEq`) | `vetting::vetters::grant::v0_1::Response` (no `PartialEq`) |
| `resend_vetter_grant() -> VetterResendResponseBody` | `-> vetting::vetters::resend::v0_1::Response` |
| `branding()` / `set_branding()` on `join_requests::CommunityBranding` | `join_requests::manifest::v0_2::CommunityBranding` |

## The guard

`vta-sdk/tests/generated_wire_types_census.rs` runs in the workspace test job. It reads every `Serialize`/`Deserialize` struct and enum in every workspace member's production source (with `syn`), and fails when a type's doc summary names a Trust Task as its payload, request, response or body **and** `trust_tasks_rs::schema_index` has a generated module for that task. It carries a baseline of 69 pre-existing hand-written types (acl, policy, config, keys, audit, rooms, vault, several VTC admin envelopes) that **only shrinks**: an entry is removed when its type is migrated, the count is asserted, and a stale entry fails.

The workspace guidelines gain the rule: Trust Task wire types come from `trust_tasks_rs::specs`; never hand-write a payload or response type for a task in the registry; keep behaviour and the rules a schema cannot state as checks over the generated types; read received JSON against the schema before parsing; specification changes land in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf first and arrive through a `trust-tasks-rs` bump. `docs/03-vtc/vetting.md` says where the wire types come from.

The conformance sweep gains witnesses for manifest 0.2 and the five `vtc/vetting/*` tasks the registry now serves, and `trust_task_manifest`'s unpublished-URI allowance for the nine vetting URIs goes to zero.

## Test evidence

Run on this branch, rebased onto `main` at 500bf059:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` | clean |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | exit 0, no warnings |
| `cargo test --workspace --exclude vtc-service --exclude vtc-client --no-fail-fast` | **4209 passed, 0 failed**, 50 ignored (118 test binaries), including the new census 3/3 |
| `cargo test -p vtc-service -p vtc-client --no-fail-fast` (with `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1`) | **1607 passed, 0 failed**, 1 ignored: units 1030 (3 binaries), integration 577 (55 binaries) |
| the same, with the real admin UI build: `admin_ui` unit tests / `routing_modes` | 8/8, 9/9 |
| `cargo test -p vta-sdk --lib --features vetting,openapi,didcomm` | 415 passed, 0 failed |
| vetting round-trips: `vetting_journey` / `join_requests` / `join_didcomm` / `vtc_client_live` | 2/2, 79/79, 3/3, 6/6 |
| `trust_task_manifest` / `openapi_snapshot` / `openapi_response_census` | 8/8, 4/4, 6/6 (the conformance sweep runs in the vtc-service units) |
| admin UI: `npm run lint` / `npm test` / `npm run build` | ok / 60 passed (9 files) / ok; `package-lock.json` unchanged |
| `check-lockfile-self-pins.sh`, `check-workspace-version-reqs.py`, `check-nitro-copies-every-member.py`, `check-authz-context-types.sh` | all exit 0 |

After the last two commits (`format: uri` enforced by hand; manifest 0.2 served without branding that breaks it), re-run on the final head:

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --all -- --check` / `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` / the four guard scripts | clean / exit 0, no warnings / all exit 0 |
| `cargo test -p vta-sdk --lib --features vetting,openapi,didcomm` | 417 passed, 0 failed (2 new: `a_format_uri_member_is_an_absolute_https_uri`, `a_listed_event_url_is_an_absolute_https_uri`) |
| `cargo test -p vtc-service --lib` | 1012 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored (new: `branding_the_manifest_cannot_carry_is_omitted_and_the_manifest_still_served`, `the_warning_names_the_member_at_fault_not_its_value`) |
| `cargo test -p vtc-service --test join_requests` / `--test join_didcomm` / `--test trust_task_manifest` | 80 / 3 / 8 passed, 0 failed (new: `a_profile_whose_event_url_is_not_an_absolute_https_uri_is_malformed`; branding PUT cases added) |
| `cargo test -p vtc-client -p cnm-cli` | 66 passed, 0 failed |
| admin UI: `npm run lint` / `npm test` / `npm run build` | ok / 77 passed / ok |

With the UI build skipped, the expected `admin_ui::tests` and `routing_modes::path_mode_admin_*` failures did not occur here, because the build directory already held a built console bundle.

## Not done

- **69 other hand-written types** for tasks that have generated modules remain, recorded in the census baseline. Migrating them is separate work.
- **`IdentityVettingEndorsement` is still hand-written**: `vetting/_shared/0.1/identity-vetting` is not a Trust Task and the codegen generates no shared definitions. Generating `_shared` definitions upstream would let it go too.
- **Extended error codes** stay hand-written constants; the codegen does not emit them.
- **The admin console's form checks** (`validateRequirements`, `validateBranding`, `buildListBody`) still restate schema rules in TypeScript for inline feedback. The daemon remains the authority; they are not generated.
- **The guard reads doc summaries**: a wire type whose summary does not name its task is invisible to it. The guidelines say to name it.
- **The OpenAPI rendering** omits `dependentSchemas`, `dependentRequired`, `not` and `propertyNames`, which utoipa cannot represent.
- **openvtc** is not updated here; the table above is what it needs.
