title: refactor(vta-sdk)!: vetting wire types come from the published trust-tasks specs (#1439)
body:
refactor(vta-sdk)!: vetting wire types come from the published trust-tasks specs (#1439)

* build(deps): bump the trust-tasks crates to 0.20.4

trust-tasks-rs 0.20.4 is the first release that carries generated Rust
types for the peer identity vetting Trust Tasks (vetting/request,
vetting/session, vetting/decline, vtc/vetting/revoke-statement,
vtc/vetting/vetters/{grant,profile,list,resend}) and for
vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.2. The binding crates (-https, -didcomm,
-proof, -capability-client) are released at the same version and move
with it.

Only the version requirements and the lockfile change; the feature set
(`validate`, `all-specs`) already covers the new spec modules.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vta-sdk)!: vetting wire types come from the published trust-tasks specs

The peer identity vetting Trust Tasks are specified in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf,
and trust-tasks-rs 0.20.4 generates their payload and response types. vta-sdk
carried hand-written copies of every one, and they had already drifted from
the specifications within the stack that introduced them.

`protocols::vetting` now re-exports the generated modules — `request`,
`session`, `decline`, `revoke_statement` and `vetters::{grant, profile, list,
resend}` — and the vetting vocabulary of `vtc/join-requests/manifest/0.2`
(`VettingRequirements`, `VettingMethod`, `VettingRelationship`,
`VettingDocumentation`, `ClaimType`). `protocols::join_requests` re-exports the
generated `manifest` module. The type URI constants are the generated types'
`TYPE_URI`. The hand-written copies are deleted.

What stays hand-written operates on the generated types:

- `CheckShape` and `read_checked`: validation against the schema each type
  embeds, taken from the JSON as received (some generated constructors
  normalise what they parse), plus the rules no schema can state — an event's
  span, `eventTo` against `eventFrom`, `minByMethod` against
  `acceptedMethods`, `joinDid` against the document issuer;
- `IdentityVettingEndorsement`, the Vetting Statement's credential body, which
  the codegen does not generate (a shared definition, not a task), now typed
  in the generated vocabulary;
- signing and verifying the card and the statement, requirements evaluation
  and digest, match codes and ticket URIs;
- the admin REST bodies for grant rows and automatic grants.

The `openapi` feature adds `vta_sdk::openapi`: transparent wrappers that let a
service document a generated type it serves over REST, with the schema
rendered from the specification's own.

`trust-tasks-rs` is now a required dependency, since the always-compiled
protocol modules re-export it.

BREAKING CHANGE: the hand-written vetting and join-manifest wire types are
removed in favour of the generated ones. The pull request lists each old path
and its replacement.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* refactor(vtc-service)!: the community speaks the generated vetting types

vtc-service, vtc-client and cnm-cli move to the generated vetting and
join-manifest types vta-sdk re-exports.

- The Trust Task handlers read vetting payloads with `read_checked`: the JSON
  is validated against the published schema before it is parsed, then the
  rules a schema cannot state are applied.
- The admin routes that carry a task's body — `POST /v1/vetting/vetters`,
  `POST /v1/vetting/vetters/list`, `GET /v1/join-requests/manifest` and
  `GET`/`PUT /v1/community/branding` — take and return the generated types.
  openapi.json describes them from the specifications' schemas, and the
  console's wire types alias those schemas instead of hand-written shapes.
- The join manifest is projected onto `manifest::v0_1::Response` and
  `manifest::v0_2::Response`. Registering an accepts criterion refuses one
  the manifest cannot publish.
- The conformance sweep gains witnesses for manifest 0.2 and the five
  `vtc/vetting/*` tasks the registry now serves, and the unpublished-URI
  allowance for them goes to zero.
- `vtc-client`'s `grant_vetter` takes the grant payload; `cnm` builds it.

BREAKING CHANGE: vtc-client's `grant_vetter`, `resend_vetter_grant`,
`branding`, `set_branding` and `VetterGrant::grant` use the generated types.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* test(vta-sdk): fail on a hand-written type for a generated Trust Task

A census over every workspace member's production source. It reads each
`Serialize`/`Deserialize` struct and enum; where the doc summary names a Trust
Task as the type's payload, request, response or body, it asks
`trust_tasks_rs::schema_index` whether that task has a generated module, and
fails if it does.

Sixty-nine hand-written types predate their tasks' generated modules (acl,
policy, config, keys, audit, rooms, vault, and several VTC admin envelopes).
They are recorded as a baseline that only shrinks: a migrated type must leave
it, and nothing may join it.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* docs: Trust Task wire types come from trust_tasks_rs::specs

The workspace guidelines gain the rule the vetting refactor applied: never
hand-write a payload or response type for a task that has a generated module;
keep behaviour and the rules a schema cannot state as checks over the
generated types; read received JSON against the schema before parsing it; land
specification changes in dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf first and take them through a
trust-tasks-rs bump. The vetting operator guide says where the wire types come
from.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vta-sdk): refuse a format: uri member that is not an absolute https URI

The vetting schemas give an event's `url`, branding's `logoUrl` and the
requirements' `governanceFrameworkUrl` `format: uri`, with `^https://` and
`maxLength: 2048`. The schema validator treats `format` as an annotation
and does not assert it, and the pattern alone admits `https://a b`, so
moving these members onto the generated types stopped refusing whitespace
and control characters. That is a gap in the validator, not a divergence
the specification asks for.

`CheckShape` now enforces the URI rule by hand (`shape::https_uri`): no
whitespace or control characters, only RFC 3986 characters with
well-formed percent-escapes, an https scheme and a host, at most 2048
characters. It runs on the vetter profile payload, the listing response,
branding and the vetting requirements, so profile publish, branding PUT
and branding storage refuse such a value, and manifest 0.2 emission
refuses stored branding that breaks it. The admin console applies the
same rule to the logo and governance framework addresses.

Regression tests cover a URL with a space, one with a control character
and an http:// URL at each layer.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* fix(vtc-service): serve manifest 0.2 without branding that breaks its definition

Manifest 0.2 emission refused stored branding that fails the manifest's
`CommunityBranding` definition with a server error. Branding is
presentation only, and the manifest is what every applicant needs to
join, so a bad logo address would have stopped every join.

Emission now leaves such branding out and serves the manifest without it,
logging a warning that names the members at fault. It names members, not
values: a value is what an admin typed and may be hostile. Storing
branding still refuses an invalid value, and the branding PUT still
answers 400, so only a row written before that check can reach
emission. No audit or telemetry event is added; the VTC has none for a
stored configuration problem, and a manifest read is not audited.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

---------

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: fix(fence): neutralise a delimiter shape that starts inside a run of angles
body:
fix(fence): neutralise a delimiter shape that starts inside a run of angles

Fence::sanitize looked for <<<, and when what followed was not the
sentinel it emitted <<< and advanced three bytes. A delimiter shape
starting one byte later was therefore never examined. Traced and then run
against main before changing anything:

  input   "<<<</UNTRUSTED-MEMORY:abc>>>"
  output  "<<<</UNTRUSTED-MEMORY:abc>>>"   byte-for-byte unchanged

The output still carries <<</UNTRUSTED-MEMORY:abc>>> starting at offset 1,
and <<<<<UNTRUSTED-MEMORY:abc>>> keeps an opening shape the same way.

This was not a working injection. The delimiters carry a per-render 48-bit
nonce from the OS RNG, and content cannot close a fence whose nonce it
cannot predict; that control held throughout. But the module documents
shape neutralisation as belt and braces on top of the nonce, and the belt
was not fastened - which is worse than not claiming it, because the claim
is what the next reader relies on.

The same function had a second defect, in the opposite direction: a
matched opener with no delimiter after it consumed everything up to the
next >>> anywhere in the text, so

  "<<<UNTRUSTED-MEMORY keep this sentence >>> and this"

lost the sentence. Sanitising is meant to defang content while leaving it
readable, not to censor it.

Both come from the same place, so both are fixed there. After a <<< that
does not begin a delimiter the scan advances one byte (<< is ASCII, so
that is always a char boundary). What gets replaced is now bounded by the
delimiter token's own grammar - <<< or <<</, the sentinel, an optional :,
at most 64 lowercase hex characters, then >>> - so a complete token is
replaced whole, and anything else that starts with the prefix loses only
the <<< and the sentinel. Text after it survives. The replacement contains
no <, and a token's fourth byte is always / or the sentinel's first
letter, so no shape can begin inside a replacement either.

Tests are the argument, per CLAUDE.md. A proptest over strings built from
{<, /, >, sentinel, :, hex, prose} asserts that no output ever contains an
opening or closing shape, that sanitising is idempotent, and that text
with no delimiter shape in it comes back untouched - that last one drawn
from a sentinel-free alphabet rather than filtered, because filtering the
first alphabet rejects almost every case it generates. Unit tests cover
both bypasses above, prose after a non-delimiter <<<, an unclosed prefix
keeping what follows, a malformed or over-long nonce losing only the
prefix, and multi-byte text around a candidate.

proptest joins dev-dependencies. Plugin and crate versions bumped in step:
the sanitizer runs in the installed binary, and claude plugin update
compares that version, not the commit.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>
author: stormer78

title: security(backup): write backup exports readable by their owner only
body:
## Summary

`cnm backup export` and both `pnm backup export` paths wrote the encrypted backup
envelope with `std::fs::write`. That creates the file at the process umask (0644
with the usual `022`), so any local user could read it. The envelope is Argon2id +
AES-256-GCM ciphertext, so exposure gives an offline password-guessing target
rather than the keys directly, but the VTA backup holds the seed and every key, and
the VTC backup holds the community signing key. The same write also silently
truncated an existing file at the path.

## Changes

### `vti-common::secure_file::write_secret_file(path, bytes)`

- `OpenOptions::create_new`: an existing path, including a symlink (dangling or
  not), is never truncated or followed. The call fails with `AlreadyExists`.
- Mode `0600` at creation on Unix, so the file is never readable by others, even
  briefly.
- `sync_all` before returning.
- On Windows, the existing owner-only DACL helper (`restrict_file_to_owner`) is
  applied after the write.
- If anything after creation fails, the file is removed: no secret left behind
  with the wrong permissions, and no stale file blocking a retry.

### `vta-cli-common::secure_file`

- Re-exports `write_secret_file`.
- `write_secret_export(path, bytes, force)`: refuses an existing file with a
  message naming `--output` and `--force`. With `force`, removes the old file and
  creates a new one.
- `check_export_path(path, force)`: the same refusal for an explicit `--output`,
  made before the password prompt and the server round-trip, so a descriptor-flow
  export isn't spent on a write that will be refused.
- `did_filename_slug(did, fallback)`: the default file name's slug comes from the
  server-supplied `sourceDid`. Only `[A-Za-z0-9._-]` is kept, the slug is capped
  at 64 characters, and it falls back to `vtc` / `vta` when nothing usable is
  left.

### Call sites

- `cnm-cli/src/backup.rs` (`cmd_export`), `pnm-cli/src/commands/backup.rs`
  (`cmd_backup_export` and `cmd_backup_export_descriptor`) use the helpers above.
- `cnm backup export` and `pnm backup export` gain `--force`.
- Docs: `docs/03-vtc/backup-restore.md` and `pnm-cli/README.md` mention the file
  mode and `--force`.

`.gitignore` is unchanged: `**.vtcbak` is already on `main` (#1435).

## Behaviour changes

- Backup files are created `0600` (owner-only ACL on Windows).
- Exporting to a path that already exists now fails unless `--force` is passed.
  Scripts that reuse a fixed `--output` name need `--force` or a fresh name.
- A default file name derived from an unusual `sourceDid` may differ from before
  (disallowed characters are dropped).

## Testing

New tests:

- `vti-common` (`#[cfg(unix)]`):
  - `write_secret_file_is_0600_under_a_022_umask`: sets `umask(0o022)`, writes,
    asserts mode `0600`, then restores the umask.

title: security(backup): write backup exports readable by their owner only (#1438)
body:
security(backup): write backup exports readable by their owner only (#1438)

`cnm backup export` and both `pnm backup export` paths (descriptor and
`--use-rest-legacy`) wrote the encrypted backup envelope with
std::fs::write. That creates the file at the process umask, 0644 by default,
so other local users could read it and try the password offline. It also
silently truncated any existing file at the path.

vti-common's secure_file gains write_secret_file: create_new (so an existing
path, including a symlink, is never truncated or followed), mode 0600 on
Unix, sync_all, and the owner-only DACL on Windows. If any step after
creation fails, the file is removed. vta-cli-common re-exports it and adds
the shared CLI pieces:

- write_secret_export: refuses an existing file unless `--force`, which
  removes it and creates a new one.
- check_export_path: the same refusal for an explicit `--output`, made before
  the password prompt and the server round-trip.
- did_filename_slug: the default file name's slug comes from the server's
  sourceDid, so keep only [A-Za-z0-9._-], cap it at 64 characters, and fall
  back to "vtc"/"vta" when nothing usable is left.

Both export commands gain `--force`.

title: security(sealed-transfer): check who sealed an admin credential before installing it
body:
## Summary

A sealed bundle is HPKE-encrypted to the consumer's request key. That keeps it
confidential, but it does not show who produced it: anyone who has seen the
bootstrap request can seal a bundle to it. Before this change, `cnm` installed an
admin credential from a bundle with no check tying it to the operator's VTA:

- the setup wizard treated an empty digest as "skip verification";
- a `DidSigned` assertion passed `open_bundle` regardless of which DID signed it,
  and no install path verified the assertion;
- the bundle's `vta_did` was never compared with the DID the operator typed;
- `SessionStore::login` stored the bundle as the session **before**
  challenge-response, so a login that failed still left that `vta_did` as the
  session later commands used.

## What producer assertion do admin credential bundles carry today?

Every path that seals an `AdminCredential` or `ContextProvision` for a consumer to
install from a file uses **`PinnedOnly` with a throwaway producer `did:key`**
(`vta_cli_common::sealed_producer::seal_for_recipient`; the private half is dropped
immediately):

| Producer | Payload | Assertion |
|---|---|---|
| `pnm auth-credential create`, `cnm auth-credential create` | `AdminCredential` | `PinnedOnly`, ephemeral did:key |
| `pnm contexts bootstrap`, `cnm contexts bootstrap` | `AdminCredential` | `PinnedOnly`, ephemeral did:key |
| `pnm contexts provision`, `pnm contexts reprovision` | `ContextProvision` | `PinnedOnly`, ephemeral did:key |
| `vta` offline context reprovision (`bootstrap_cli::run_context_reprovision`) | `ContextProvision` | `PinnedOnly`, ephemeral did:key |
| `vta bootstrap seal` (Mode C) | any payload file | `PinnedOnly`, ephemeral did:key |
| TEE `POST /bootstrap/request` | `AdminCredential` | `Attested`; consumed only by `pnm bootstrap connect`, which verifies the quote |
| provision-integration (`#sealed-transfer-0`) | `TemplateBootstrap` / `AdminRotation` | `DidSigned`, producer = VTA DID; not an admin-credential install path |

So for admin credentials the out-of-band digest is the only anchor that exists
today, and an expected VTA DID is enough for the `DidSigned` case. No
`--expect-producer-did` flag is added.

## Changes

### `vta-cli-common::sealed_consumer`

- `open_admin_credential(bundle_path, config_dir, expect_digest, expected_vta_did)`
  opens the bundle and calls `verify_admin_bundle`, which matches the verified
  assertion exhaustively (the same pattern as `verify_template_bundle` in
  `vta-service`):
  - `PinnedOnly`: accepted only with `expect_digest`;
  - `DidSigned`: accepted only if the producer DID equals `expected_vta_did` and
    the Ed25519 signature verifies. Any other signer is refused, with or without
    a digest. Only `did:key` producers can be verified here;
  - `Attested`: refused;
  - when `expected_vta_did` is given, `credential.vta_did` must equal it.
- The request secret is removed only after the bundle is accepted, so a rejected
  bundle does not use up the pending request. `open_armored_bundle` keeps its
  existing behaviour for inspection.
- `normalize_expected_digest`: 64 hex characters, trimmed, lower-cased.

### `cnm-cli`

- `setup` / `community add`: the digest prompt requires 64 hex characters (the
  "empty = skip" option is gone), and the credential is checked against the VTA
  DID typed in the same wizard step.
- `auth login --credential-bundle`: flags go through `validate_digest_flags`, and
  the bundle is checked against the community's configured `vta_did`.
  `--no-verify-digest` stays, but only a bundle signed by that DID is then
  accepted.
- `bootstrap open` (inspection) is unchanged, including `--no-verify-digest`.

### `pnm-cli`

- There is no `pnm auth login --credential-bundle` subcommand in the code (the
  README and `phase5-cutover.md` still mention one). The install-shaped path is
  `pnm bootstrap open --out`, which writes the credential for file-based
  consumers. It now goes through `verify_admin_bundle`, checked against
  `--expect-vta-did` when given. Without `--out`, `bootstrap open` only inspects
  and is unchanged.

### `vta-sdk`

- `SessionStore::login` runs challenge-response first and saves the session only
  on success. An existing session under the same key is left untouched by a
  failed login.

## Behaviour changes

- The `cnm` wizard no longer accepts an empty digest.
- `cnm auth login` refuses a credential whose `vta_did` differs from the
  community's configured VTA DID, and refuses `--expect-digest` combined with
  `--no-verify-digest`.
- `cnm auth login --no-verify-digest` fails for every bundle `pnm`/`cnm` produce
  today, because they are `PinnedOnly`.
- `pnm bootstrap open --out --no-verify-digest` no longer writes a credential
  file for a `PinnedOnly` bundle.
- If `cnm auth login` opens a bundle but authentication then fails (e.g. the VTA
  is unreachable), no session is stored. The request secret has already been
  used by then, so a retry needs a new bootstrap request and bundle.

## Testing

New tests in `vta-cli-common::sealed_consumer`. Each seals a real bundle to a real
bootstrap request:

- `admin_credential_signed_by_an_unexpected_did_key_is_rejected`: a correctly
  signed `DidSigned` assertion from a freshly generated did:key, with the
  credential pointing at that key's own DID. Refused against
  `did:webvh:victim` without a digest, with the bundle's own digest, and with no
  expected DID at all. The request secret is still present afterwards.
- `admin_credential_signed_by_the_expected_vta_is_accepted`: producer DID ==
  expected VTA DID, valid signature, no digest. Accepted, and the secret is
  consumed.
- `did_signed_by_another_key_in_the_vta_name_is_rejected`: the assertion names the
  expected VTA but is signed by a different key.
- `pinned_only_admin_credential_needs_the_digest`: refused without a digest (secret
  kept); accepted with the digest as an operator might type it (upper-case,
  surrounding whitespace).
- `admin_credential_for_a_different_vta_is_rejected`: valid digest, but
  `credential.vta_did` differs from the expected DID.
- `attested_admin_credential_is_rejected`.
- `expected_digest_must_be_64_hex_characters`.

`cnm-cli::setup`: `digest_prompt_rejects_empty_input`,
`digest_prompt_accepts_only_a_sha256_hex_digest`.

`vta-sdk/tests/session_store.rs`:

- `login_against_an_unreachable_vta_persists_no_session`: `login` against
  `http://127.0.0.1:1` errors, and `has_session` / `loaded_session` show nothing
  was stored.
- `failed_login_keeps_the_existing_session`: an earlier session under the same
  key survives a failed login.
- `login_propagates_challenge_failure` now also asserts no session is stored.

Run locally (macOS, rustc 1.98.1):

- `cargo fmt --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p vta-sdk -p vta-cli-common -p cnm-cli -p pnm-cli --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo clippy -p vta-sdk --features session,test-support --lib --test session_store -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p vta-cli-common -p cnm-cli -p pnm-cli`: all pass (vta-cli-common
  107, cnm-cli 28, pnm-cli 62).
- `cargo test -p vta-sdk --features session,test-support`: 686 passed, 0 failed,
  10 ignored, including `tests/session_store.rs`.

`cargo clippy -p vta-sdk --features session,test-support --all-targets -- -D warnings`
fails with `items_after_test_module` at
`vta-sdk/src/protocols/acl_management/swap.rs:118`. This change doesn't touch that
file, and the same command fails the same way on `main` (5a6d4923).

Not exercised end to end: an interactive `cnm setup` run, and a `DidSigned` bundle
from a `did:webvh` producer. Those can't be verified without DID resolution and
are refused.

title: security(sealed-transfer): check who sealed an admin credential before installing it (#1437)
body:
security(sealed-transfer): check who sealed an admin credential before installing it (#1437)

HPKE sealing makes a bundle confidential to the consumer, but anyone who has
seen the bootstrap request can seal a bundle to it. cnm installed an admin
credential from such a bundle without anything tying it to the operator's
VTA: the setup wizard accepted an empty digest as "skip verification", a
self-signed DidSigned assertion passed open_bundle, and the bundle's vta_did
was never compared with the DID the operator typed.

vta-cli-common gains open_admin_credential and verify_admin_bundle, which
every install path now goes through:

- PinnedOnly is accepted only with the out-of-band digest. This is the form
  every admin credential sealed today takes (pnm/cnm `auth-credential
  create` and `contexts bootstrap`, pnm `contexts provision|reprovision`,
  vta's offline reprovision and `bootstrap seal`), with a throwaway producer
  did:key.
- DidSigned is accepted only when the producer DID is the expected VTA DID
  and the signature verifies. A valid signature from any other DID is
  refused, with or without a digest.
- Attested is refused; attestation is verified by `pnm bootstrap connect`.
- When an expected VTA DID is known, the credential's vta_did must match it.
- The request secret is consumed only once the bundle is accepted, so a
  rejected bundle does not use up the pending request.

Call sites:

- `cnm setup` / `cnm community add` require a 64-hex digest and check the
  credential against the VTA DID typed in the same wizard.
- `cnm auth login --credential-bundle` validates the flag combination and
  checks against the community's configured VTA DID. With
  `--no-verify-digest` only a bundle signed by that DID is accepted.
- `pnm bootstrap open --out` applies the same check before writing the
  credential file (checked against `--expect-vta-did` when given). Inspection
  without `--out` is unchanged.

SessionStore::login now saves the session only after challenge-response
succeeds. Before, it stored the bundle first, so a login that failed still
left the bundle's vta_did as the session every later command used, replacing
any working session under the same key.

title: feat(vetting): guided join, vetter directory and profile, QR tickets, grant checks, resend and branding
body:
Stacked on #301 (`feat/community-context-actions`). The applicant and vetter experience for the vetter registry in VTI #1430 (`feat/vtc-vetter-registry`; contract `CONTRACT-vetter-registry.md`; specs trustoverip/dtgwg-trust-tasks-tf#453).

## What

- **VTI patches** now take `feat/vtc-vetter-registry`, the top of the VTI vetting stack (#1425–#1430).
- **Guided join.** When you enter a community's DID, the join flow finds out whether that community vets its members. If it does, a page says what it requires in plain words: how many statements, which methods count, how long a statement stays valid, which claims vetters check, and whether an invitation is also needed. The page also shows this persona's application if one exists. It offers three ways on:
  - **start or continue the application** — you choose the persona and context, and the Vetting page opens on the application with its next step highlighted;
  - **join anyway** — the community refers the request to its moderators;
  - **cancel**.
  
  An application that already meets the published requirements joins as its own persona, and the page says its statements go with the request.
- **Find vetters** (`v` on an application): a community's vetter directory, for communities you are applying to or have joined.
  - Filters: language, country, region, city, method, event date range and event name.
  - Each result shows the display name beside the DID, languages, location, methods, accepted documentation, availability, upcoming events and how to get a ticket.
  - Results are paged by cursor and kept only in page state.
  - **Ask this vetter** fills in the request form and says a ticket is still needed, quoting the vetter's contact hint.
- **Your vetter profile** (`p` on Tickets), for communities where you hold a live vetter grant.
  - Fields: listed or unlisted, display name, languages, location, methods, accepted documentation (defaulting from `VetterPolicy`), availability, contact hint, and events you can add, edit and remove.
  - Everything is checked with the SDK's `check_shape` before it is sent.
  - The last profile sent is kept in the book, together with the community's answer or its `notEligible` refusal.
- **QR tickets.** The Tickets tab shows the selected ticket's `vetting-ticket:` link as a QR code drawn in Unicode half-blocks and sized to the window. `u` copies the link.
  - The link carries the scanned form (ticket id and secret); the short code stays for reading aloud.
  - Pasting a link into the request form fills in the vetter and the ticket. A link for another community is refused with a clear message.
- **Revocation check.** After a vetter's acceptance and eligibility presentation verify, the grant's `credentialStatus` is checked in the background with a bounded HTTPS fetch. The request then shows one of:
  - "named a vetter until …";
  - "the community has revoked this vetter's grant";
  - "could not check whether the grant was revoked".
- **Grant resend** (`g` on Tickets). Where you are an active member without a live vetter credential, you can ask the community to send it again. A `notGranted` refusal is shown in plain words.
- **Community branding.** The manifest's `branding` is kept. An accent swatch (●) in the community's own colour sits beside its name on the Vetting page, the Communities panel and the join page. `displayName` is used as a fallback name.
- **Docs.** As-built notes in `docs/design/vetting-process.md` §6.1, §7, §7.1, §8.2, §10.3 and §12.3, plus decisions D25–D29.

## How

### `openvtc-core/src/vetting/`

- **`queries.rs` (new).** Questions put to a community — manifest, list, profile, resend — are remembered in memory by request document id (`#[serde(skip)]` on the book).
  - An answer, or a `trust-task-error` threaded on a question, becomes a `CommunityAnswer` for whoever asked.
  - A `trust-task-error` that answers nothing we asked still falls through to the join handler.
  - Questions unanswered after 30 s expire.
  - `refusal_words` turns `notEligible`, `notGranted`, `permissionDenied` and `malformedRequest` into sentences a person can act on.
- **`registry.rs` (new).** `ProfileDraft`, `EventDraft` and `DirectoryFilter` turn typed text into `VetterProfileBody` / `VetterListBody`. They name the field a person got wrong and leave every bound to the SDK's `check_shape`.
  - `VetterProfileRecord` keeps the last profile sent, as JSON, with a `ProfileState` of Sent, Stored or Refused.
- **`guide.rs` (new).** `describe_requirements` renders the requirements as sentences.
- **`status.rs` (new).** `GrantCheck::run` calls `check_credential_status` with an `https`-only fetch: 5 s to connect, 10 s overall, at most three redirects and 6 MiB. Its errors tell an unreachable host from an HTTP error from a body that is not a status list.
- **`inbound.rs`.** Handles the list, profile and resend responses and refusals.
  - A manifest now answers the question that asked for it and teaches the community's branding.
  - A verified eligibility presentation whose grant names a status list returns a `GrantCheck`; one with no status entry is recorded as "could not check".
- **`book.rs`.**
  - `Knowledge`: vets, does not vet, or never asked.
  - `KnownCommunity` with `Branding` and `parse_accent`.
  - `adopt_known_requirements` and `resend_candidates`.
- **`applicant.rs`.** `GrantStatus` on each request, `ticket_from_uri` (refuses a link for another community), and `NextStep`.
- **`tickets.rs`.** `Ticket::uri`.
- **`wire.rs`.** Request builders for the list, profile and resend tasks.

### `openvtc`

- **Join flow.**
  - `join_flow.rs`: `JoinEntry` (Fresh / Resume), `JoinExit::AwaitRequirements`, `resume_for`, `vetting_view`, `apply_for_vetting`, plus `continue_join` and `open_invitation_choice` pulled out of the existing arms.
  - `ui/pages/join_flow/vetting_requirements.rs`: the page itself.
  - `state_handler/mod.rs`: the runtime loop's wait, the resume, and a single join entry point at the loop tail.
- **Vetting page.**
  - `vetting_actions.rs`: directory, profile form, resend, ticket paste, `apply_answers`, `expire_queries`, `spawn_grant_check` / `GrantChecked`, `focus_application`.
  - `main_page/content.rs`: state for the directory, profile and event forms, ticket links and next steps.
  - `components/vetting_panel.rs`: rendering.
  - `components/qr.rs`: the half-block renderer.
- **`background_dispatch.rs`.** A separate `VettingStatus` domain.
- **`message_dispatch.rs`.** `InboundEffects` carries `vetting_answers` and `vetting_grant_checks`.
- **Branding.** Shown in `main_page/mod.rs` and `communities_panel.rs`.

## Notes for review

- **How the guided path learns requirements without hanging.** The join sub-loop cannot receive the manifest reply: its `select!` has only the action and interrupt arms, and inbound messages are read by the runtime loop's own arm, which is parked while `join_flow` runs.
  - The flow first uses what the book already knows.
  - If the book does not know, it sends `manifest/0.2` (the send itself is bounded at 15 s) and returns `JoinExit::AwaitRequirements`.
  - The runtime loop keeps the join screen up in an "asking" state and keeps reading inbound messages.
  - It re-enters the flow — through a single entry point at the loop tail — when the manifest arrives, when the community refuses or sends an unreadable answer, or after 15 s via the existing 5 s sweep.
  - While it waits, `j` joins without waiting and Esc cancels.
  - Every wait ends on a message or a deadline.
  - The degraded (State A) loop has no inbound arm, so there the flow uses the book only.
- **The manifest question comes from the active persona.** A DIDComm Trust Task needs an authenticated sender, so the community learns that persona's DID. Please say if you would rather it came from a persona with nothing linked to it.
- **A first profile is unlisted.** Listing is opt-in (design §7).
- **The profile is persisted as JSON** rather than the SDK type, because `VetterProfileBody` is `deny_unknown_fields` and a newer build's record must not break an older build's config load.
- **Directory entries show the published display name beside the DID, never instead of it.** The branding `displayName` comes after the membership's own name and a verified agent name. Neither is an agent name, so the agent-name rule does not apply.
- **The accent swatch and the QR code use literal colours**, with comments explaining why: the swatch is data about the community, and a scanner needs black on white. The QR code uses error correction M (L if needed) and a quiet zone of 4, narrowing to 2 or 1 before telling you the width it needs.
- **Grant checks are spawned without the busy guard, in their own domain.** They start from inbound messages rather than a person, so they must never release or block the `Vetting` domain a person's send holds.
- **`GrantCheck::run` gives the fetch closure a future that owns its arguments.** A future holding the borrowed `&str` across `.await` is not `Send` for every lifetime the SDK's `AsyncFn(&str)` may be called with. A core test asserts `Send`.
- **Nothing was run against a live VTC.** The wire shapes are covered by message-level tests using the SDK types on the registry branch.
- **`cargo-deny` is not installed here.** `qrcode` 0.14 with default features off is MIT OR Apache-2.0 and has no dependencies, so `deny.toml` needs nothing.
- **Networking rules.**
  - R1.2: every new outbound path is bounded — status fetch 5 s connect / 10 s total; manifest send 15 s; the join wait 15 s; question expiry 30 s.
  - R1.4: there is no polling loop.
  - R6.4: refusals, unreadable answers and transport failures each have their own wording.
  - R3.6: the task types and shapes are the SDK's on `feat/vtc-vetter-registry` at 94440966.

## Test evidence

Stacked PRs get no CI, so this is what CI runs, run locally on the head of this branch:

- `cargo fmt --all --check` — clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- `cargo test --workspace` — 17 binaries, 1269 passed, 0 failed, 17 ignored
- `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features` — 17 binaries, 1269 passed, 0 failed, 17 ignored
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS=-D warnings cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` — clean

New tests:

- **Core, message level (`vetting/tests.rs`):**
  - profile published, then stored or refused `notEligible`;
  - directory answer: an unasked page, another community, a refusal, an unrelated error left for the join handler, an unreadable answer;
  - resend answered, or refused `notGranted`;
  - a manifest answering the question that asked, with branding;
  - a verified grant with a status list handed on for checking, and one without a status list;
  - a scanned ticket link, and a link for another community;
  - the next step.
- **Core, unit:**
  - `queries` — matching, expiry, refusal words;
  - `registry` — drafts, dates, locations, filters, the persisted record;
  - `guide` — sentences, durations;
  - `status` — https only, error classification against wiremock, `Send`;
  - `book` — knowledge, branding, accent parsing, adopted requirements, resend candidates;
  - `tickets` — the link round trip.
- **TUI:**
  - key routing: directory results versus filters, Tickets tab `p`/`g`/`u`, profile event rows and ticks, pasting a ticket link, and the join vetting page in every phase;
  - outcomes: a directory page lands only in the view that asked, refusals are shown plainly, unanswered questions expire, a revoked grant is recorded and shown, the profile form opens on what was last sent;
  - join flow: `resume_for`, `vetting_view`;
  - rendering: the QR renderer's half-block mapping, sizing and too-narrow behaviour; the join page's copy.

title: refactor(persona): one word for a persona [on hold — awaiting vocabulary]
body:
> **On hold.** The functional half — the ACL grant the pane needs — moved to
> #279 so it isn't blocked by a naming decision. What's left here is vocabulary,
> and you're settling the canonical terms; I'll redo this sweep against whatever
> lands rather than merging a word that's about to change.

## What this was going to do

Rename the pane's "face" to **persona**, on the evidence that "face" appears
nowhere else in the ecosystem:

- the Trust Tasks spec, the VTA, the SDK, `pnm persona binding set --persona-did`
- the console pane shipped this week (nav "Persona"; sections "Attributes",
  "Profiles", "What each persona presents")
- this repo's own `PersonaRecord` / `persona_ref` / `persona_did`
- (the 69 "face" hits in the browser plugin are all `surface` / `interface`)

**Not "profile"** — that already names the thing a persona *presents*. You bind
a profile to a persona; the reverse is not a sentence, and reusing the word
would collide head-on with `persona/profile/*`.

The overload "face" was invented to dodge is real — the `persona/*` task family
spans the DID and everything above it — but it's a prose problem with a prose
fix: say "persona DID" where a sentence has to be unambiguous, exactly as `pnm`'s
own help does.

Also renames `ContentPanelState::personas` → `identity`, so the list can take the
name it should have had (`identity.personas`, not `personas.personas`) — that
part is independent of which noun wins, since the menu entry has read
"My Identity" since #277.

## When the vocabulary lands

The sweep is mechanical (~112 occurrences, mostly prose) and I'll re-run it
against the agreed terms. Worth deciding at the same time: whether the menu
entry stays "My Identity", and whether the tab keeps the plural noun.

title: feat(communities): delete a community's context, choose a persona's context, per-community device access
body:
Stacked on #298 (`feat/community-contexts`). Draft.

## What

Three things a holder can now do with a community's own VTA context, from the communities panel and My Identity:

1. **Delete a finished community's context** (`D` on a left / withdrawn / rejected / removed / expired membership). Everything the delete removes is shown, the holder types `DELETE`, then the context and its subtree are deleted — together with the persona that joined from it, when that membership was the persona's only use.
2. **Choose a standalone persona's context.** Creating a persona under My Identity offers what a join offers: a new sub-context named from the label (editable), a context already in use, or the top context. The DID and its keys are minted there and recorded as the persona's `origin_context_id`.
3. **Give a device or agent access to one community** (`g` on a membership with its own context). Paste a `did:key`, name it, choose an expiry (1 / 7 / 30 / 90 days); list and revoke grants. Grants also show in the panel's detail block.

## How

### Deleting a context
- `community_context::deletable_context` (core, pure) decides. It refuses: the top context (never offered, never sent), a membership still live, and any other use of the context — another membership, **another persona's keys** (`origin_context_id`), a vetting application (`applications[].context_id`) — naming each use.
- **The persona that joined from the context.** Joining mints the persona into the community's context, so the common case is a context holding the keys of the membership's own persona. If this finished membership is that persona's **only** use — no other membership of any status, no vetting application (in any context), and not the active/default persona (`Config::active_persona`, else `active_identity()`) — the persona and the finished membership record are deleted with the context, in the same confirmed action. Any other use refuses, naming the persona and each use (`DeletionRefusal::PersonaInUse`).
- `preview_context_deletion` calls `contexts/list` to find the sub-contexts, then `contexts/preview-delete` for the context **and each sub-context** (the VTA's preview covers only the context named, while the delete cascades). Either the whole subtree is previewed or it fails — a preview missing a sub-context would look complete.
- The panel lists every key, DID, ACL entry removed, ACL entry narrowed and DID template, grouped by context, and then — explicitly — the persona (label and DID) and the membership record when they go too, saying that the persona can no longer be used anywhere and that its `did:webvh` is removed from its host through the VTA, or stays published there if the host cannot be reached. Without a persona it says the membership record is kept. The confirmation must be typed exactly (`DELETE`); paste is not accepted into it.
- On Enter the decision is taken **again** against the current config and must be the same one the holder was shown (same context, same persona or none).
- `delete_community_context` then removes the persona's DID first through the VTA's existing `webvh/dids/delete` (`VtaClient::delete_did_webvh` — the removal persona deletion already uses: revokes credentials the VTA issued to the DID and deletes its log at the hosting server). It must go first: the context cascade only drops the VTA's own record of the DID, after which nothing could remove it from its host. If the VTA refuses the DID, nothing is deleted. Then `contexts/delete` with `force: true`.
- Applied on the loop: the persona is forgotten locally through the existing persona-deletion cleanup (`DidDeleteOutcome`) as soon as its DID is gone — even if the context delete then fails, since it can no longer be used; its listener is removed; the membership record is deleted and its session torn down through the runtime loop (`AfterApply::Deregister`); membership `sub_context_id` / application `context_id` naming the context are cleared so the startup registration job does not recreate it.

### Persona context choice
- `create_persona::context_choice` / `chosen_context` reuse `community_context::context_options` and `new_context_id`; `suggested_context_id` (core) names the new sub-context from the label, falling back to `persona` for a label with nothing slug-able.
- The overlay gains a `Context` phase (Label → Context → Working). The mint job runs `ensure_context` first, then `create_did_via_server` in the chosen context; `MintedPersona::persist` records `origin_context_id`.

### Device access
- New core module `openvtc_core::community_access`. There is no pairing flow in OpenVTC to extend (`devices.rs` only registers this install), and the VTA's device slice is "the device-facing half of an `AclEntry`" — `device/register` refuses a DID not already in the ACL. So a grant is a plain `acl/grant/0.1` entry, after which the device enrols itself as any device does.
- **Role: `application`.** The least-privileged role that can *act* in a context: `monitor` has no capabilities and `reader` only reads the vault and memory (neither can sign or present); `application` adds `sign`, `signTrustTask`, `proxyLogin`, `roomPresent`; `initiator` would add `keyMint`, `vaultWrite`, `deviceAdmin`, and `admin` would let the device manage the context's ACL. It is also the role the VTA's own device enrolment uses. Scope is the community's context (covering its subtree, nothing beside it).
- Grant: `acl/grant/0.1` with `scopes: [<community context>]`, `expiresAt`, and a label naming device and community. `ensure_context` runs first.
- **One entry per DID.** If the DID already holds an entry the grant is refused, naming what it holds — never widened, which would share one expiry across communities and could extend an entry made for another purpose or role.
- List: `acl/list/0.1` in the **subtree** direction (`list_acl_in_direction(.., Subtree)`), then filtered locally to entries that name a context at/below the community — so a VTA that ignores `direction` still never shows (or offers to revoke) OpenVTC's own top-context admin entry. OpenVTC's own DID is excluded outright.
- Revoke: re-reads the entry (`acl/show`), then `acl/revoke` if it names only this community, or `acl/update` narrowing it to its other contexts.
- Scope is decoded from `(role, allowed_contexts)` together in one function (`act_scope`, mirroring `vti_common::acl::act_scope_for`, which the SDK does not expose for a listed entry). Nothing tests `allowed_contexts.is_empty()`.
- `parse_device_did` catches pasted DID URLs, truncated keys, non-`did:key` DIDs, and OpenVTC's own DID before a grant is attempted (Ed25519, P-256, secp256k1 multicodecs).

### Plumbing
- All VTA calls are background jobs in a new `DispatchDomain::CommunityAccess` (preview, delete, list, grant, revoke — serialised so a listing can't overtake the change it follows) plus `DeviceGrantSweep` (grants for every membership context once a run, after context registration finishes). Outcomes apply on the loop thread; a stale outcome for a closed or different view is dropped.
- `Action::CommunityContext(CommunityContextAction)`: view-only variants go through the shared nav reducer; the rest through `runtime_actions`. The degraded (State A) loop lists them with the other community-only actions.
- Errors say which kind of failure it was (`vta_failure`): unreachable vs. session not accepted/not allowed vs. request rejected (R6.4). All SDK calls carry the SDK's finite timeouts (R1.2).
- `ContextOption::summary` moved from the vetting panel into core so the persona overlay shares it; `join_flow::context_taken` now delegates to `community_context::context_claimed`.

## Notes for review
- The DID removal is reported by the VTA as success even when its hosting daemon rejected the delete (`webvh/dids/delete` puts that in the result body, which `delete_did_webvh` discards); the preview therefore says the DID "stays published there if the host cannot be reached" rather than promising it is gone.
- Deleting a context is not announced to the community; it removes the holder's own keys, DIDs, access and faces at their VTA.
- The preview→delete window is re-checked locally (config), not re-previewed at the VTA; a device granted in between would be removed by the cascade (the VTA removes entries scoped only to the deleted context).
- `application` could be narrowed further with `capabilities` on the grant; which capabilities a given agent needs is its own contract, so the role default is used and narrowing is left for a follow-up.

## Test evidence (local — stacked PRs get no CI)
Run on the branch head exactly as `.github/workflows/ci.yml` does (with `VTC_SKIP_ADMIN_UI_BUILD=1`):

| Step | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo fmt --all --check` | clean |
| `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo test --workspace` | ok — openvtc 513 unit, openvtc-core 615 unit, every integration suite, doctests; 0 failed |
| `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features` | ok — same totals; 0 failed |
| `cargo doc --workspace --no-deps` | ok, 0 warnings |
| `cargo test -p openvtc-core --test community_context_e2e -- --ignored` | ok, 2 tests against a real in-process VTA (below) |

The ignored MockVta tests check the VTA contract rather than assuming it (R3.6):
- **grant, list, preview, revoke, delete** — grant with scope + expiry, one-entry-per-DID refusal, subtree listing that excludes a sibling, preview naming the sub-context and the device's entry, revoke, cascade delete that keeps the sibling, top context refused.
- **context with its persona** — a persona `did:webvh` minted into a community context (stub webvh host) appears in the preview, is removed through `webvh/dids/delete` before the context is deleted, and is gone from the VTA afterwards; the top context is refused before the DID is touched.

New tests:
- **core** `community_context`: deletion refusals (top, live, other membership, another persona's keys, vetting application); the persona taken along when this membership is its only use, with the consequences naming its DID; the persona kept and the refusal naming each use (another membership of any status, a vetting application in another context, the active persona); membership kept without a persona; segment-aware descendants; preview lines; exact confirmation; label-based context suggestion; VTA error kinds; option summary. `community_access`: `did:key` parsing, grant wire shape, expiry, label bounds, role+scope decode, subtree filtering (ancestor, sibling-prefix, super-admin, acts-nowhere, own DID excluded), narrow-vs-delete revocation, expiry display.
- **TUI** key routing (`D`/`g` gating, deletion view owns keys and refuses paste, device list/form/revoke keys, grant-form paste, persona context phase); nav reducer; loop dispatch (persona-only-use opens the preview with the persona marked, persona used by another membership or active is refused by name without a VTA call, word + fresh re-check before delete, top context refused for device access, bad DID caught before a grant); outcome application (stale preview dropped; context + persona + membership removed together with the session teardown requested; persona forgotten but membership kept when the DID went and the context delete failed; nothing changed when the DID removal was refused; records let go of a deleted context; grant/revoke messages and list refresh; sweep never overwrites a newer listing); panel rendering (hints, unread vs. none, preview items, persona + DID + consequences, role text); persona context choice and resolution.

title: feat(communities): delete a community's context, choose a persona's context, per-community device access (#301)
body:
feat(communities): delete a community's context, choose a persona's context, per-community device access (#301)

* feat(communities): delete a community's context, choose a persona's context, give devices access

A community's own VTA context could be created but not cleaned up, a
standalone persona was still minted into the top context, and there was no
way to let a second device act for the holder in one community only.

Deleting a context. A membership that is over (left, withdrawn, rejected,
removed, expired) offers "D: delete context" on the communities panel. What
else uses the context is checked first — another membership, any persona's
keys, a vetting application — and named in the refusal. Otherwise the VTA's
contexts/preview-delete is read for the context and for every sub-context the
delete cascades to, all of it is shown, the holder types DELETE, the use check
runs again, and contexts/delete runs with force. The records then let go of
the context so the registration job does not recreate it. The top context is
never offered and is refused before the VTA is asked.

A standalone persona's context. Creating a persona under My Identity now asks
where it lives, as a join does: a new sub-context named from its label
(editable), a context already in use, or the top context. The context is made
to exist, the DID and its keys are minted in it, and it is recorded as the
persona's origin.

Device access per community. "g: devices" opens a community's device access:
paste a did:key, name it, pick an expiry (1, 7, 30 or 90 days), and the VTA
gets an acl/grant entry with the application role scoped to that context
alone. Grants are read with acl/list in the subtree direction, shown on the
panel's detail, and revoked with acl/revoke — or narrowed with acl/update when
the entry also names contexts outside the community. application is the
least-privileged role that can sign and present; reader cannot sign, and
initiator/admin would let the device mint keys or manage access. A DID that
already holds an entry is refused rather than widened. Scope is decoded from
role and contexts together, never from an empty list alone.

All VTA calls run as background jobs; outcomes are applied on the loop thread.
Core decisions live in openvtc-core (community_context, community_access) with
unit tests, plus an ignored MockVta test exercising grant, subtree list,
preview, revoke and cascade delete against a real VTA.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

* feat(communities): delete a context together with the persona that joined from it

Joining mints the persona into the community's context, so the usual context
held that persona's keys and deleting it was always refused — and the persona
could not be deleted first, because persona deletion counts finished
memberships too.

When the finished membership is the persona's only use — no other membership
of any status, no vetting application, not the active or default persona — D
now deletes the context, that persona, and the membership record in one
confirmed action. The preview names the persona and its DID, says it can no
longer be used anywhere, and that its did:webvh is removed from its host
through the VTA or stays published there if the host cannot be reached. Any
other use of the persona refuses, naming the persona and each use.

The persona's DID goes first, through the VTA's existing webvh/dids/delete
(the removal persona deletion already uses): the context cascade only drops
the VTA's record of the DID, after which nothing could remove it from its
host. If the VTA refuses the DID, nothing is deleted. Once the DID is gone the
persona leaves the account through the existing persona cleanup, even if the
context delete then fails; the membership's session is torn down by the
runtime loop.

The decision is core and pure (deletable_context, ContextDeletion,
PersonaInUse) with tests for the allowed and every refused case; the outcome,
dispatch and preview are tested in the TUI; an ignored MockVta test mints a
persona DID in a community context and deletes it with the context.

Signed-off-by: Glenn Gore <glenn.g@affinidi.com>

title: feat(tui): live theme switching, auto light/dark, accessible themes, NO_COLOR and export
body:
Builds on #299. A running TUI now picks up theme changes live. It adds an `auto` theme that follows the terminal's background, four accessibility themes, `NO_COLOR` support, themed command-line output, and `openvtc theme export`.

## What
- **Live switching.** A running TUI redraws within about a second when any of these change:
  - `tui.toml` (for example, `openvtc theme set` run in another terminal);
  - the `user/` theme file in use;
  - Omarchy's current theme (`~/.local/state/omarchy/current/theme.name`, or the older `~/.config/omarchy/current/theme` link);
  - the in-use Omarchy theme's `colors.toml`.
- **`auto`.** Follows the terminal's background. OpenVTC asks the terminal with OSC 11 before the alternate screen is entered, then falls back to `COLORFGBG`, then to dark.
  - `openvtc theme set auto [--dark <id>] [--light <id>]` sets the two themes. They are kept in `tui.toml` as `auto_dark` / `auto_light` (defaults `openvtc` and `catppuccin-latte`).
  - The picker lists **Auto (follow terminal)** first. Settings shows `Theme: Auto — <theme>`.
- **Accessibility built-ins:**
  - `high-contrast-dark` and `high-contrast-light`: every colour ≥ 7:1 against the background.
  - `colourblind-dark` and `colourblind-light`, in Okabe–Ito hues: every colour ≥ 4.5:1. The light variant darkens each hue until it reads on white.
- **`NO_COLOR`** (set and non-empty). Every role and the background become the terminal default. Roles stay apart through modifiers:

  | Role | Modifier |
  |------|----------|
  | accent | bold |
  | danger | bold + underline |
  | warning | underline |
  | success and selections | reversed |
  | highlight | italic |
  | muted | dim |

  `console`/`dialoguer` output is uncoloured too, and the picker says themes are not being drawn.
- **`OPENVTC_THEME=<id>`** chooses a theme for one session. An id that can't be loaded is reported, and the chosen theme is used instead.
- **Themed pre-TUI output.** `style(..).color256(CLI_*)` becomes `style(..).themed(CLI_INFO | CLI_ERROR | CLI_CAUTION | CLI_EXAMPLE)` across `main.rs`, `health_cmd.rs` and `theme_cmd.rs`.
  - It uses the active theme's role colour: 24-bit when `COLORTERM` is `truecolor`/`24bit`, otherwise the nearest xterm-256 index. The default theme's accent maps back to 69, the old `CLI_BLUE`.
  - `theme::init` runs straight after argument parsing, before anything is printed.
- **Export.** `openvtc theme export <id> --format openvtc|base16|omarchy|alacritty|kitty [--output <path>]`.
  - It prints bare to stdout by default.
  - Omarchy with `-o` writes a theme directory (`colors.toml`, plus `light.mode` for light themes), unless the path ends in `.toml`.
  - Omarchy output uses the key set of Omarchy's current `colors.toml` (checked against `basecamp/omarchy` `themes/tokyo-night`).
  - Colours a format needs that OpenVTC doesn't have (the ANSI 16, base16 shades) are derived from the roles.
- **Import warning.** `theme import` now warns when a theme's text is under 4.5:1 against its background.
- **Docs.** `docs/themes.md` covers all of the above.

## How
- **`theme/live.rs`.** `Watcher::check(&self) -> Option<Update>` stamps `tui.toml` and the files the followed theme is read from (mtime, size, link target), and loads the theme only when something differs. It mutates nothing; `accept` commits the update.
  - The UI loop (`ui/mod.rs`) runs `check` on `spawn_blocking` from a one-second `interval` and gets the result back over a channel. The render loop never touches the file system.
  - The loop skips checks while `SettingsMode::ThemePicker` is open. It also drops results from any check that overlapped the picker being open (a picker-epoch counter), so a preview is never overridden and the change is found again once the picker closes.
  - The loop now redraws only when something happened (poll ticks do not redraw). The harness confirms zero bytes are written while idle.
- **Choice semantics.** A theme chosen while running (in the picker, or via `theme set`) replaces the session's theme, including one chosen by `OPENVTC_THEME`. Other edits to `tui.toml` redraw nothing. Under `auto`, changing `auto_dark`/`auto_light` redraws.
- **Atomic `tui.toml` writes.** `tui.toml` is now written via a temp file and rename. `catalog::read_choice` returns `None` for unparseable TOML, so a half-saved file never flips the theme. A half-saved theme file keeps the current theme until it is saved whole.
- **`theme/terminal.rs`.** Opens `/dev/tty`, enters crossterm raw mode, and writes `OSC 11 ?` followed by DA1 (`ESC [ c`). It reads with `poll(2)` until the DA1 reply arrives, capped at 500 ms. It parses `rgb:` with 1–4 hex digits per channel. On non-Unix it returns nothing and falls back to `COLORFGBG`.
- **`theme/export.rs`.** `render` / `write`.
- **`theme/mod.rs`.**
  - `Role`, `Palette::get`, and `Mode::of_background` (moved from `import.rs`; it now also handles named colours).
  - `rgb` (xterm values for named and indexed colours) and WCAG `contrast`.
  - `no_color`, `paint_without_colour`, `display_name`, `init`.
- **`catalog.rs`.** `AUTO_ID`, `Choice` (`theme`, `auto_dark`, `auto_light`; `auto` can't pick itself), `read_choice` / `choice`, `remember_auto`, `resolve`, and `sources`. `load("auto")` loads the resolved theme under the id `auto`. `load_selected` and `selected` are gone; `theme::init` covers them.

## Notes for review
- **Dependency.** Adds `libc = "0.2"` as a Unix-only direct dependency, for `poll(2)` with a timeout. It was already in `Cargo.lock` beneath crossterm and console, so the only lock change is the edge. There is no file-watcher dependency: polling stats a handful of files.
- **When the terminal is asked.** Only when `auto` is the choice in effect at startup, and never under `NO_COLOR` or when stdin/stdout isn't a terminal.
  - This keeps a startup delay, and a slow link's late reply landing in the passphrase prompt, away from people who don't use `auto`.
  - The trade-off: choosing Auto in the picker of a session that didn't start with it uses `COLORFGBG`/dark until restart, and the status message says so.
  - The terminal can't be asked mid-session, because crossterm's event reader would take the reply as keys.
  - The DA1 sentinel means terminals that answer return within milliseconds. Only a terminal answering neither query waits the full 500 ms.
- **`NO_COLOR` and `success`.** Success is reversed because success + bold is this codebase's selected-row style. The trade-off is that success text elsewhere (e.g. the picker's "Theme" heading) is also reversed.
- **CLI colours on light themes.** Pre-TUI output uses the theme's role colours on the terminal's own background. A light theme's accent may be darker than ideal on a dark terminal. `auto` avoids the mismatch.
- **Crossterm and `NO_COLOR`.** Crossterm independently drops colour when `NO_COLOR` is non-empty. Our paint does the modifier mapping, so both agree.
- **Scope.** No service calls are added or changed, so the networking rules (R1.2/R1.4/R6.4) don't apply.

## Tests
- **Painting.** `theme::tests`: `NO_COLOR` modifiers per role (panels' own modifiers are kept), `rgb` for named and indexed colours, WCAG figures, mode from background.
- **Contrast.** `builtin::tests::text_is_readable_on_every_built_in_background`: text ≥ 4.5:1 for every built-in; every colour ≥ 7:1 (high contrast) or ≥ 4.5:1 (colourblind).
- **Terminal.** `terminal::tests`: OSC 11 replies with ST, BEL, and 1- and 2-digit channels; DA1 detection; `COLORFGBG` forms.
- **Catalogue.** `catalog::tests`: `auto` resolves and keeps its id, `auto` can't pick itself, `sources` for user and Omarchy themes, half-written `tui.toml`.
- **Live.** `live::tests`:
  - a user file edit, including a half-saved file;
  - a theme chosen elsewhere replacing an `OPENVTC_THEME` session, while unrelated `tui.toml` edits redraw nothing;
  - `auto_dark`/`auto_light` changes;
  - Omarchy switching via `theme.name`, and via the legacy symlink (Unix);
  - edits to Omarchy's `colors.toml`.
- **Export.** `export::tests`:
  - every built-in with a background round-trips through `openvtc`, `base16`, `omarchy`, `alacritty` and `kitty` via the importers (same palette and mode);
  - files written to disk are recognised by `import::from_path`;
  - an Omarchy dir gets `light.mode`, and it is removed when overwritten with a dark theme;
  - the default theme exports on black.
- **Settings picker.** The picker test now also checks Auto is listed first, previews under the id `auto`, and is remembered.
- **CLI.** `set auto --dark --light`, `export --format -o`, the default format, an unknown format refused.
- **Colours.** Nearest-256 mapping (`#5f87ff` → 69, `#61afef` → 75).

Local results, matching `.github/workflows/ci.yml`:
- `cargo fmt --all --check`: clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test --workspace`: openvtc 505 passed, 1 ignored (needs Neovim); openvtc-core 551; did-git-sign 5.
- `cargo test --workspace --no-default-features`: pass.
- `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --workspace --no-deps`: clean.

**CLI smoke test, `OPENVTC_CONFIG_PATH` in a scratch directory:**
- `theme set auto --dark nord --light high-contrast-light` writes `theme`/`auto_dark`/`auto_light`.
- `set nord --dark …` and `--dark nosuch` are refused with a clear message.
- `theme list` shows Auto first and the four new built-ins.
- `OPENVTC_THEME=bogus` reports it was ignored, and `list` notes the override.
- `export high-contrast-dark` to all five formats, then `theme import` of each file, gives five identical palettes.
- A low-contrast Alacritty import warns (1.3:1).
- `NO_COLOR=1 CLICOLOR_FORCE=1` emits no escapes. `COLORTERM=truecolor` emits `38;2;…`; without it, `38;5;110`.

**TUI end-to-end, a Python pty harness driving the real binary (13/13):**
- `auto` sends OSC 11; answering white draws High Contrast Light's `#ffffff`.
- No bytes are written while idle.
- `openvtc theme set dracula` from outside redraws in Dracula.
- A `user/` theme chosen from outside is drawn, and an edit to its file is drawn.
- Non-auto themes never query the terminal.
- `omarchy/current` draws Omarchy's current theme, and rewriting `theme.name` switches it.
- `OPENVTC_THEME=nord` overrides the choice.
- `NO_COLOR=1` emits no 24-bit colour but does emit bold/reverse; an empty `NO_COLOR` still draws colour.

title: feat(tui): themes — built in, your own, Omarchy's, and imported from Neovim and friends
body:
Adds themes to the OpenVTC TUI. People can pick one of several built-in themes, follow or import Omarchy themes, import themes from Neovim, base16/base24, Alacritty, Kitty or Ghostty, and make their own.

## How it works
Every panel already drew with seven colour **roles**, the `COLOR_*` constants: accent, success, warning, danger, text, muted and highlight.
- **Painting:** after each frame, `theme::paint` swaps each role for the active theme's colour. It also paints the theme's background, where the theme has one.
- **No panel changes:** panels, and the open PRs that touch them, carry on using the roles.
- **Default unchanged:** OpenVTC's own theme maps every role to itself, so an unthemed TUI looks exactly as before.

## Choosing
- **Settings → Theme.** Moving through the list previews each theme on the whole screen. Enter keeps it and Esc puts back the previous one. `c` copies the highlighted theme to edit, and `r` reloads after an edit.
- **CLI.** `openvtc theme list | set <id> | import <source> [--name] [--use] | new <name> [--from <id>]`. It runs without opening a profile.
- **Where it's saved.** The choice is kept in `~/.config/openvtc/tui.toml`, which honours `OPENVTC_CONFIG_PATH`. It is the person's setting, not the account's, so every profile shares it.

## Sources
| Id | Source |
|----|--------|
| `openvtc` (default), `catppuccin-mocha`, `catppuccin-latte`, `dracula`, `gruvbox-dark`, `nord`, `tokyo-night` | built in |
| `user/<name>` | the person's theme files in `~/.config/openvtc/themes/` |
| `omarchy/current` | the current Omarchy theme, followed as it changes |
| `omarchy/<name>` | an Omarchy theme, read in place from `~/.config/omarchy/themes`, `~/.local/share/omarchy/themes` or `/usr/share/omarchy/themes` |

**Import formats** (`openvtc theme import …`):
- base16 and base24 YAML schemes, in both the current and the legacy layout.
- Omarchy theme directories. These use `colors.toml`, or the `alacritty.toml` older themes carry, with `light.mode` marking a light theme.
- Alacritty, Kitty and Ghostty colour files.
- `nvim:<colorscheme>`, which runs `nvim --headless` with the person's own config, so plugin-managed colorschemes work. It reads back the highlight groups every colorscheme defines. `--clean` skips the config.

An import writes an ordinary OpenVTC theme file, commented so it can be edited by hand. A role that file leaves out keeps OpenVTC's own colour. `docs/themes.md` covers the format and how each source maps onto the roles.

## Notes for review
- **Dependency:** adds `toml = "1"`, which was already in `Cargo.lock` transitively.
- **Unthemed output:** CLI output printed before the TUI starts (prompts and errors) still uses the terminal's colours.
- **Paint cost:** `paint` does one pass over the frame's cells, and returns immediately for the default theme.
- **Settings order:** the Theme row sits at index 7, after Import. Token management and Wipe move down one row. No test depended on those indices.
- **Base branch:** this branch is off `main`. The vetting stack (#292–#298) keeps using the role constants, so it themes without changes.

## Tests
- **Painting:** roles are swapped, other colours are kept, and the default theme changes nothing.
- **Colour parsing:** every form the formats use.
- **Readers:** each format, including the partial-theme fallback and a native write→read round trip.
- **Neovim:** mapping a highlight report onto roles, and refusing unknown or unsafe colorscheme names.
- **Catalogue:** install / remember / load, Omarchy discovery (the person's copy shadows the system's; the current theme is followed), fallback to the default, and path traversal refused.
- **Settings picker:** previews, cancels, copies and applies.
- **CLI:** `theme` subcommand parsing.

Run locally:
- `cargo test --workspace`: all pass (openvtc 485, plus 1 ignored test needing Neovim, which passes locally).
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

**End-to-end smoke test, in a scratch config directory** (Neovim 0.12):
- imported Omarchy's real `tokyo-night` directory and a real tinted-theming `gruvbox-dark-hard` base16 scheme;
- imported `nvim:retrobox` (with the user config) and `nvim:habamax --clean`;
- ran `theme new`, `theme set` and `theme list`;
- checked `nvim:nosuchscheme` is refused.

title: security(vta-sdk)!: vet DID-advertised VTA endpoints and bind cached tokens to their origin
body:
## Why

A VTA's REST base URL comes from the `#vta-rest` service in its DID document (or is synthesized from the DID's domain). Until now it was used as-is: any scheme, any host, with embedded credentials. Every later authenticated call went there. Separately, `SessionStore::ensure_authenticated` returned the cached access token whatever base URL it was called with. If the advertised endpoint changed, a live bearer token for the original VTA went to the new host.

While fixing that, the existing foreign-fetch guard (`vta_sdk::http::guard_public_url`, which fronts the VTC recognise/present paths and vta-vault status lists) turned out to pass IPv4-mapped IPv6 loopback, carrier-grade NAT addresses (including a cloud metadata address) and `localhost`. It also did no DNS-level check. A unit test against `main` confirmed all three literal cases.

## What changes

### `vta-sdk::http`
- **One classifier.** `classify_ip` / `classify_host` (with `IpClass` / `HostClass`) cover:
  - IPv4 private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, `0/8`, broadcast, multicast, documentation, benchmarking and reserved space;
  - IPv6 loopback, unspecified, ULA, link-local, site-local, multicast, documentation, Teredo, discard and local-use NAT64;
  - IPv4 embedded in IPv6 (mapped, compatible, NAT64 `64:ff9b::/96`, 6to4), classified by the embedded address;
  - named cloud-metadata addresses (`fd00:ec2::254`, `100.100.100.200`);
  - local-only names (`localhost`, `*.localhost`, `*.local`, `*.internal`, `*.home.arpa`, single-label names) and metadata hostnames.

  It mirrors `affinidi-did-web`'s classifier. A comment marks it for replacement by the shared `affinidi-net-guard` crate once that is published.
- **`guard_public_url`** uses the classifier. Its signature is unchanged.
- **`foreign_fetch_client`** now installs a DNS resolver that fails closed if any answer for a name is non-public, and connects only to the vetted addresses. It also sets `no_proxy()`, so a proxy cannot resolve the name on its behalf.
- **`guard_vta_endpoint(url, EndpointPolicy)`**:
  - `https` required; `http` only to `localhost`, `127.0.0.0/8` or `::1` (the same predicate as `vta-webvh`'s webvh client).
  - Always refused: userinfo, other schemes, link-local and metadata addresses and names, unspecified, broadcast, multicast, documentation, benchmarking and reserved addresses, and IPv6 forms embedding a non-public IPv4 address.
  - RFC 1918, ULA, CGNAT and local-only names are accepted only when the private-endpoint policy is enabled. The refusal names the opt-in, and URL credentials are never echoed.
- **`EndpointPolicy::process_default()`** enables private endpoints when `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS` is truthy or the binary called `set_allow_private_endpoints(true)`.
- **`rest_client()`** follows a redirect only while scheme, host and port stay the same as the original request. Otherwise the `3xx` is returned to the caller.

### `vta-sdk::session`
- Every REST URL from `resolve_vta_endpoint_with_resolver` (and so `resolve_vta_endpoint` and `provision_client::resolve_vta`), `resolve_vta_url` and the forced-REST path of `connect_with_transport` passes `guard_vta_endpoint`. That covers both the advertised `#vta-rest` and the URL synthesized from the DID.
  - A refused URL is an error, never a silent fallback. This includes a document that also advertises TSP/DIDComm, since the REST URL is carried in those variants.
- New `resolve_vta_endpoint_with_resolver_and_policy` takes an explicit policy.
- The persisted session gains `token_origin` (serde-defaulted). It is set wherever a token is stored (`login`, `ensure_authenticated`). A cached token is returned only when the requested base URL has the same origin; otherwise the session re-authenticates. Sessions saved before this change have no origin and re-authenticate once.

### CLIs
- `cnm` and `pnm` gain a global `--allow-private-endpoints` flag (also read from `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS`).
- `cnm backup`, `cnm audit verify` and `pnm bootstrap connect` use `vta_sdk::http::rest_client()` instead of a bare `reqwest::Client::new()`, and read responses through `read_body_capped`:
  - backup: 64 MiB, matching the VTC's backup-import request cap;
  - audit verify and bootstrap: 1 MiB.
- `cnm-cli/clippy.toml` and `pnm-cli/clippy.toml` add a `disallowed-methods` entry for `reqwest::Client::new`. Clippy picks config up from each crate's directory, so other crates are unaffected.

## Operator-visible behaviour changes
- A VTA whose DID document advertises a private-network REST endpoint (for example `https://10.0.0.5`) is now refused by default. Pass `--allow-private-endpoints` or set `VTA_ALLOW_PRIVATE_ENDPOINTS=1`. This applies to any SDK consumer resolving VTA endpoints, not only the CLIs.
- Plain `http://` endpoints are refused unless the host is loopback. Local-dev setups using `http://localhost:…` or `http://127.0.0.1:…` keep working.
- A cached token is no longer reused against a different origin; the CLI re-authenticates instead.
- `cnm backup` and `cnm audit verify` now have the SDK's request timeouts (30 s by default, `VTA_REST_TIMEOUT_SECS` to raise).
- Foreign fetches (status lists, recognition) refuse hostnames that resolve to non-public addresses, and no longer go through `HTTP(S)_PROXY`.
- `--url` overrides are unchanged: an operator-supplied URL is not run through the endpoint guard.

## Merge note
A separate change reorders `SessionStore::login` so the session is saved only after authentication succeeds. This PR touches `login` only to add `token_origin: None` to the initial `Session` and to record `session.token_origin` next to the token. Expect a small textual conflict there; keep both.

## Tests
- `vta-sdk/src/http.rs`:
  - classifier block/allow vectors, URL canonicalisation vectors, local-name and scheme vectors;
  - stubbed DNS answers (mixed, mapped, NAT64, empty), and a real `localhost` lookup refused by the resolver;
  - `guard_vta_endpoint` accept, always-refuse and opt-in cases, and credential redaction;
  - a same-origin redirect is followed and a cross-origin redirect is not (the target sees no request).
- `vta-sdk/src/session.rs`: legacy session without `token_origin` loads; origin normalisation; forced-REST URL vetting over a seeded resolver.
- `vta-sdk/tests/session_store.rs`:
  - seeded DID documents through `resolve_vta_endpoint_with_resolver`: the metadata URL is refused even with the opt-in; a userinfo URL is refused without echoing credentials; `https://10.0.0.5` is refused unless opted in; `http://127.0.0.1:8100` is accepted; a bad REST URL beside a DIDComm mediator is refused;
  - a cached token is reused for the same origin (including a `/v1` path) but not for a different origin.
